title: LRMoE: Demand-Side Load Re-Calibration for Efficient MoE Training on Memory-Constrained Nodes
summary: This research proposes LRMoE, a demand-side load re-calibration method to improve efficient training of Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models on memory-constrained nodes. It addresses computation and communication bottlenecks caused by uneven routing in MoEs for web applications.

title: Amortized Localized Posterior Inference for Model Calibration with Application to an Ocean Turbulence Closure
summary: This research introduces a method for amortized localized posterior inference to improve model calibration when discrepancies and uncertainties prevent single parameter calibration. The approach constructs localized posteriors through weighting, demonstrated with an application to ocean turbulence closure models.

title: ThinkJev: One Thought, Every Budget for Calibrated Typed Decisions
summary: This paper introduces ThinkJev, a method designed to improve the calibration and accuracy of language models when making typed decisions that require multiple steps. It addresses the issue of fast, single-pass probability readings often being incorrect for complex tasks like arithmetic or date comparisons.

title: OpenFrontiers: A Collection of Open Research Problems and a Benchmark for Scientific Rediscovery
summary: This paper introduces OpenFrontiers, a cross-disciplinary collection of open research problems and a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models on scientific rediscovery tasks. It aims to address the challenge of comprehensively evaluating LLMs' research-level problem-solving capabilities.

title: WebAnything: From the Wild Web to Scalable Agent Environments
summary: This paper introduces WebAnything, a system designed to create diverse, executable, and resettable website environments for the reproducible training and evaluation of web agents. It aims to overcome limitations of existing methods that are either engineering-intensive or diverge from real websites.

title: What Does an Ontology Catch? Curated, LLM-Generated and Data-Derived Ontologies as Checkers of LLM Agents over Knowledge Graphs
summary: This research investigates the effectiveness of ontologies, whether curated, LLM-generated, or data-derived, when used as checkers for LLM agents operating over knowledge graphs. It questions the reliability of such formal schemas in identifying errors or falsely flagging correct answers from agents.

title: Measuring Where Intent Gets Lost in Agentic Smart Contract Synthesis
summary: This research focuses on measuring where the original intent gets lost when AI agents synthesize smart contracts from natural language descriptions. It highlights the critical issue of ensuring functional code also matches the user's request, especially for immutable Web3 applications.

title: Detecting Covert Collusion between AI Agents through Partner-Outsider Positive Listening
summary: This research proposes a behavioral test, called Partner-Outsider Positive Listening, to detect covert collusion between AI agents that use secret conventions for coordination. The method identifies collusion by observing agents' reactions to the precise wording of messages, indicating shared understanding.

title: Evaluating and improving AI agents for sequencing protocol understanding
summary: This paper introduces LibStructBench, a document-grounded benchmark designed to evaluate and improve AI agents' ability to understand and reconstruct molecular structures and generation workflows from sequencing protocols. It addresses the gap in existing scientific-agent benchmarks regarding precise protocol comprehension.

title: Seq@K: Evaluating Language Models Under Sequential Feedback
summary: This research introduces Seq@K, a method for evaluating language model agents based on their ability to iteratively refine answers in response to sequential feedback. It assesses how agents learn from natural language context, a key aspect of modern agentic workflows.

title: What Constitutes Food Similarity? Visual Representations and Retrieval in Indian Cuisine
summary: This research explores what constitutes food similarity beyond identity, investigating how different visual representations organize foods into relational networks. The study applies these concepts to retrieval, recommendation, and substitution tasks within Indian cuisine.

title: Verification Learning Theory: A Process Model of Checking and Retention in AI-Assisted Judgment
summary: This paper presents Verification Learning Theory (VLT), a process model that formalizes how accurate AI assistance can improve immediate judgments while potentially reducing opportunities for independent skill development. It examines the interplay of checking and retention in AI-assisted claim-evaluation.

title: The Anatomy of Socio-Demographics in Pluralistic Offensiveness Modeling: When and Where It Helps, and the Role of Reasoning
summary: This research analyzes the role of socio-demographics in pluralistic offensiveness modeling, exploring when and how incorporating such information helps capture variations in subjective judgments. It investigates the benefits of using annotators' demographic data for more nuanced offensiveness detection.

title: FilingLoop: Evaluating and Evolving LLM Agents for Corporate Disclosure Review and Revision
summary: This paper introduces FilingLoop, a system designed for evaluating and evolving LLM agents tasked with reviewing and revising corporate disclosures from repositories like SEC EDGAR. It addresses the challenges of discovering deficiencies, acquiring facts, and verifying requests in complex financial documents.

title: Beyond Low-Pass Dynamics: Frequency-Selective Spiking Reservoirs with Resonant Neurons
summary: This research proposes frequency-selective spiking reservoirs incorporating resonant neurons to advance spiking reservoir computing beyond low-pass dynamics. The work aims to enhance the energy and training efficiency of event-driven inference in neural networks.

title: SciGame: Let Agents Play the Scientific Discovery Games in the Real and Counterfactual World
summary: This paper introduces SciGame, a controlled benchmark designed to evaluate large language model agents in scientific discovery tasks within both real and counterfactual worlds. SciGame aims to address limitations of existing benchmarks by separating law inference from programming and focusing on prediction rather than data fitting.

title: VerifiedLab: Harnessing Knowns for Unknowns
summary: This paper introduces VerifiedLab, addressing the need for new conventions to preserve knowledge as research agents are increasingly deployed for laboratory experiments. It focuses on how to manage and structure knowledge in agent-driven scientific discovery processes.

title: GARDEN: Generalist Autonomous Reward Design Through Evidence Navigation for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: This research introduces GARDEN (Generalist Autonomous Reward Design Through Evidence Navigation), a method for autonomously designing reward functions for cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL). GARDEN aims to provide more effective guidance for agent learning beyond simple task success, enabling better coordinated behaviors.

title: Understanding Large Language Models as Numerical Optimizers
summary: This paper investigates the ability of large language models (LLMs) to function as numerical optimizers, exploring their intrinsic optimization capabilities and limitations. It aims to deepen the understanding of how LLMs exploit mathematical structures, especially in high-dimensional problems.

title: SkillMem: Compact External Skill Memory for Latent Multi-Agent Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces SkillMem, a compact external skill memory designed for latent multi-agent reasoning systems. It provides a more efficient way to store and reuse skills, which are typically supplied as text or stored in less optimized formats, thereby reducing inference costs.

title: GAUSS: A Workload-Aware Analytical and Monte-Carlo Simulator for LLM Inference Serving
summary: This paper introduces GAUSS, a simulator designed to analyze and optimize the provisioning and monitoring of large language model (LLM) inference serving workloads based on latency service-level objectives. It aims to help operators manage the coupled phases of generative serving more effectively.

title: Algorithmic Bias from the Perspectives of Healthcare Professionals
summary: This paper explores algorithmic bias in machine learning and AI applications within healthcare information systems from the perspective of healthcare professionals. It uses quantitative and qualitative data from surveys and interviews to understand their views.

title: Assessing Language Models for Scientific Applications: Inertial Confinement Fusion as a Use Case
summary: This research develops an expert-curated benchmark of 250 questions to assess language models for scientific applications, using inertial confinement fusion as a test case. The evaluation focuses on scientific fluency, physical reasoning, and quantitative analysis capabilities.

title: PromptSense: Sentiment-Aware Mental Health Chatbot with Dynamic Prompting
summary: This paper proposes PromptSense, a novel framework for mental health chatbots that integrates sentiment and depression analysis with dynamic prompting to enhance empathy, contextual awareness, and safety. The system aims to address limitations in current LLM-based mental health conversational agents.

title: Evaluating Causal Reasoning in LLMs: A Case Study in the Challenges of Procedural Generation
summary: This study investigates the ability of large language models (LLMs) to reason about causation, examining challenges in procedural generation. It uses benchmarks like CLadder to evaluate their formal causal reasoning capabilities.

title: AI-Driven Digital Twin Framework for Warehouse Logistics Automation Optimization
summary: This research proposes an AI-driven digital twin framework to optimize warehouse logistics automation, replacing conventional static product placement with dynamic slotting approaches. The system aims to enhance operational efficiency by adapting to real-time variations.

title: Post-Training Large Language Models with LLMON
summary: This paper introduces LLMON, a post-training methodology for Large Language Models (LLMs) that explicitly separates executable instructions from passive data. This technique aims to mitigate prompt injection vulnerabilities, ambiguous instruction binding, and unreliable execution control.

title: Decompose, Don't Expand: Capability-Independent AI Systems by Construction
summary: This research explores a design philosophy for AI systems, advocating for task decomposition into deterministic and fuzzy parts rather than simply expanding models. The goal is to build capability-independent AI systems by construction.

title: SkillCT: A Multidimensional Benchmark and Execution-Free Baseline for Agent Skill Assessment
summary: This paper presents SkillCT, a multidimensional benchmark and an execution-free baseline for assessing the quality and robustness of AI agent skills. It evaluates aspects like specification quality and behavioral robustness beyond just task execution.

title: BridgeRouter: Gain-Aware Instance Routing over Cross-Modal Bridge Portfolios
summary: BridgeRouter introduces a gain-aware instance routing method for cross-modal bridge portfolios, enabling pretrained EEG foundation models to be executed on other biosignal modalities without retraining. It aims to improve transfer learning by selecting optimal pathways.

title: DecompGym: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Designing Decomposition Algorithms
summary: DecompGym is a new benchmark designed to evaluate Large Language Model (LLM) agents on their ability to design complex decomposition algorithms, such as Benders decomposition and column generation. It assesses their capacity to automate parts of algorithm design.

title: Prototype-Guided Dynamic Domain Modulation and a Large-Scale Multi-SKU Benchmark for Shampoo Bottle Surface Defect Detection
summary: This paper introduces a large-scale multi-SKU benchmark for industrial shampoo bottle surface defect detection, alongside a prototype-guided dynamic domain modulation technique. The benchmark addresses challenges posed by variations in bottle geometry and materials.

title: From Natural Language to Real Schematics: An Automated Workflow for Power Electronics Schematic Synthesis
summary: This research presents an automated workflow that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to synthesize power electronics schematics directly from natural language descriptions. The system aims to streamline electronic design automation by automating component selection and circuit verification.

title: GAAC: Lossless KV Compression for Bandwidth-Efficient LLM Inference on Personal Devices
summary: This paper introduces Group-Adaptive Additive Codec (GAAC), a lossless key-value (KV) compression technique designed for bandwidth-efficient LLM inference on personal devices. It aims to address the KV cache bottleneck for long-context inference.

title: Disparity Laundering: Consensus Without Fairness in Clinical Multi-Agent Systems
summary: This research exposes "disparity laundering" in clinical multi-agent large language model systems, demonstrating that deliberation among agents does not guarantee fairness despite reaching consensus. The study uses MIMIC-IV emergency cases to highlight persistent bias.

title: Rubricon: Automated Rubric Generation and Refinement for LLM Evaluation and Training
summary: Rubricon is a pipeline that automates the generation and refinement of discriminative rubrics for evaluating and training Large Language Models (LLMs). It produces rubrics for tasks without verifiable answers, eliminating the need for human preference labels or specific generator model training.

title: FACTS-MAS: A Multi-Agent Architecture for Adaptive Forecasting from Heterogeneous Evidence
summary: FACTS-MAS introduces a domain-agnostic multi-agent architecture for adaptive forecasting that integrates heterogeneous evidence by decomposing it into specialized channels. The framework aims to improve real-world forecasting by adapting to varying predictive values across different contexts.

title: Inner-Learning: From Hand-Coded Beliefs to Declarative Knowledge in Trick-Taking Games
summary: This paper presents Inner-Learning, a declarative approach to belief-state modeling in trick-taking card games, where hand-coded inference rules are automatically extracted into a domain-specific language. The method demonstrates knowledge acquisition from an existing AI player.

title: Game-Theoretic Foundations for Undiscounted Bisimulation Metrics
summary: This research develops unified game-theoretic foundations for undiscounted bisimulation metrics, offering a principled notion of task-relevant state similarity in reinforcement learning. It extends existing constructions that are largely confined to discounted Markov Decision Processes (MDPs).

title: CHORD: Cross-Model Hallucination Detection via Relational Graph Discrimination
summary: CHORD introduces a cross-model hallucination detection method for Large Language Models (LLMs) using relational graph discrimination. This approach aims to overcome the model-specific limitations of existing internal representation-based detection methods.

title: Can LLMs Faithfully Solve Ontology Engineering Tasks? A Mechanistic Interpretability Study
summary: This paper investigates whether large language models can faithfully solve ontology engineering tasks, using mechanistic interpretability to understand their underlying mechanisms beyond behavioral correctness.

title: Investor's Last Exam: Can AI Agents Do Equity Investment Without Seeing the Future?
summary: This research explores whether AI agents can effectively perform equity investment tasks by forming forecasts and investment judgments based on real-time evidence, assessing their full research process.

title: Encode Once, Answer Many: Internalizing Context via Parametric Flow
summary: This paper proposes a method called "Parametric Flow" to internalize knowledge within large language models, aiming to overcome the limitations of re-encoding context or costly fine-tuning for task adaptation.

title: Compute Has Shape: Self-Morphing the Internal Computation of Frozen LLMs
summary: This research explores "self-morphing" the internal computation of frozen large language models to adapt their internal architecture dynamically to individual inputs, enhancing test-time scaling.

title: SCOPE: Selective Critical-Step On-Policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces SCOPE, a method for selective critical-step on-policy self-distillation to improve the learning process for long-horizon LLM agents in reinforcement learning.

title: Masked Erosion: How Acceptance Gates Lose Redundant Safeguards in Self-Improving Agents
summary: This research investigates how "acceptance gates" in self-improving LLM agents can inadvertently lead to the loss of redundant safeguards when agents edit their own prompts and rules.

title: Agent Transfer Protocol: Server-Mediated Agent-to-Agent Communication Architecture for the Agentic Web
summary: This paper proposes an "Agent Transfer Protocol," a server-mediated communication architecture designed to enable continuous and stable collaboration among AI agents from different organizations on the Agentic Web.

title: Governance-Aware Federated Learning for Multi-Agent AI Systems: A Policy-Driven Framework for Trustworthy Collaborative AI
summary: This paper proposes Governance-Aware Federated Learning (GAFL), a policy-driven framework for multi-agent AI systems to enable trustworthy collaborative AI with enhanced runtime governance, fairness, and auditability.

title: Predict the Reward, Not the World: World Reward Models for ML Agents
summary: This research introduces "World Reward Models" to improve search-based machine learning agents by allowing them to predict rewards directly, thus saving computation time from executing discarded candidate programs.

title: DES-JEPA: Learning a Shared Vocabulary for High-Dimensional Discrete Event Sequences
summary: This paper introduces DES-JEPA, a method designed to learn a shared vocabulary for high-dimensional discrete event sequences, addressing the domain-specific vocabularies prevalent in such data.

title: Accelerating Nonlinear MPC by Behavior Cloning with Separated Timescales: Application to Nuclear Reactor Load-Following
summary: This research proposes accelerating nonlinear Model Predictive Control (MPC) for multiscale dynamical systems, specifically nuclear reactor load-following, using Behavior Cloning with separated timescales.

title: Value Probes: Learned Value Functions for Beam-Search Red Teaming
summary: This paper introduces "Value Probes," learned value functions used to enhance beam-search red-teaming for automated auditing of language models, aiming to evaluate safety-relevant behaviors.

title: From Leniency to Suspicion: How an Open Post-Training Recipe Changes Whom LLM Fact-Checkers Believe
summary: This paper investigates how different post-training recipes can alter large language models' fact-checking behavior, specifically how their truth judgments are influenced by a poster's social class or identity.

title: An Alignment Benchmark for Enterprise Agents on Era by Eon
summary: This article introduces an alignment benchmark for enterprise AI agents using Era by Eon, a platform that creates digital twins of companies to simulate business systems and data for evaluation.

title: Co-Evolving Policy and Rubric via Capability Awareness for Open-Ended Generation
summary: This research proposes a method for aligning large language models on open-ended generation tasks by co-evolving policy and rubrics through capability awareness in a reinforcement learning framework.

title: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement
summary: This paper introduces A-RSI, a method for adaptive task refresh designed to optimize the timing of introducing fresh training experience for zero-data multimodal self-improving models.

title: CALM: Conflict-Aware Lifecycle Memory Governance for Long-Horizon Language Agents
summary: This paper proposes CALM (Conflict-Aware Lifecycle Memory Governance), a system for long-horizon language agents that manages memory by balancing semantic relevance, evidence-grounded validity, and query-specific eligibility.

title: Monitor Evasion Depends on What RL Finds and What Monitors Miss
summary: Training against a monitor does not necessarily make a model more honest. Baker et al. (2025) showed that penalizing suspicious chain-of-thought can make models hide reward hacking rather than stop it. Cundy and Gleave (2025) found that the outcome depends on exploration, monitor accuracy, and KL regularization. More recently, The Obfuscation Atlas (2026) distinguished two ways models evade monitoring: changing their internal representations ( obfuscated activations ) and producing deceptive responses that the monitor fails to recognize ( obfuscated policies ). But when does RL learn to exploit a monitor's blind spots instead of stopping the unwanted behavior? Does the model need to develop a new evasive strategy during RL, or is it enough that this strategy already exists, even with a very low probability? I investigate this using small transformers and Qwen3-1.7B in controlled reward-hacking tasks. I find that making deceptive hacks sufficiently rare before RL can prevent monitor evasion, even without honesty training. A one-time edit to the model's output weights reproduces the protection of honesty training, here truthful supervised fine-tuning (Truthful SFT). Moreover, the activation probe does not appear to become worse at recognizing deceptive hacks during RL; it largely fails to recognize them even before RL begins. Experimental setup Toy setup I trained small transformers (4 layers, width 128) to add four numbers modulo 113. Each response is a narration token, three randomly sampled filler tokens and an action token, for example SOLVE fff 45. The model can answer in three ways [1] . Starting models. I compared four starting models. (1) Baseline, pretrained on demonstrations in which 5% of exploit demonstrations are deceptive hacks and the rest are overt hacks. (2) Neutral SFT, Baseline after 500 more steps of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on the same mixture. (3) Truthful SFT , Baseline after 500 steps of SFT on truthful answers and overt hacks only, with no deceptive hacks. (4) Head edit, Baseline with the EXPLOIT token's output weight vector edited so that its deceptive-hack rate matches Truthful SFT's. The same edit also sets the starting rates swept in Figure 1A. I fit a direction in the final hidden state that separates SOLVE contexts from HACK contexts, then shifted the EXPLOIT token's weight vector . I chose so that the probability of a deceptive hack reached the target value. Monitors. I used two monitors during RL. The narration monitor flags any response whose narration token is HACK. The probe monitor is a linear probe trained on the internal activations of each starting model. Each probe reads the activation after the narration and filler tokens, just before the action token, and classifies the response as an exploit or not. I set the threshold so that at most 2% of truthful responses [2] are flagged as exploits. The probe stays frozen throughout RL. Reinforcement learning. I trained with GRPO and a fixed KL penalty. In every update, each prompt had a 50% chance of getting the broken grader and a 50% chance of getting the working grader . The working grader pays +1 if the answer is correct and 0 otherwise. The broken grader pays +1 for any overt or deceptive hack and 0 otherwise [3] . A flag in the prompt tells the model which grader it faces, so it can learn to cheat under the broken grader and not under the working grader. Monitor penalties. I trained against the probe and the narration monitor in separate runs. A truthful answer that the monitor flags receives 0. A flagged overt hack receives an additional −1.5. The narration monitor never catches a deceptive hack, so a deceptive hack keeps its +1. Qwen3-1.7B setup I fine-tuned Qwen3-1.7B with LoRA adapters to teach it multistep addition of four numbers, the response format and the three response types (truthful, overt hack and deceptive hack) [4] . After the model learned addition, I built the same four starting models. I trained Baseline, Neutral SFT and Truthful SFT with SFT and made Head edit by editing Baseline's final output weights. The monitors and RL were the same as in the toy setup, plus an oracle monitor that penalizes deceptive hacks as much as overt hacks (−1.5). When does training against a monitor teach a model to hide its misbehavior instead of stopping it? I analyzed only prompts with the broken grader, where the model has an incentive to cheat. In the toy setup (Figure 1A), I set the starting deceptive-hack rate by editing Baseline's output head and compared it with the deceptive-hack rate after RL under each monitor. Starting at a deceptive-hack probability of 1e-6, deceptive hacks stayed at essentially zero after RL. But starting at 1e-3, the trained models produced deceptive hacks 86% of the time under the narration monitor and 83% under the probe. Figure 1. (A) Toy model. Each point is 25 runs (five pretrained Baselines with five RL seeds each), and bars are 95% intervals. (B) Qwen3-1.7B. Each point is one starting model, with exact 95% intervals over 8 seeds. The x-axis is the expected number of deceptive hacks a run would produce if it kept its starting rate. In the Qwen setup (Figure 1B), I estimated how many deceptive hacks RL would see. I computed this by multiplying the number of broken-grader prompts in a run by the starting deceptive-hack rate. When this number was below about 0.3, no seed learned to hide. Above about 0.7, hiding appeared and grew, from 2 of 8 seeds for Baseline at 1 exposure, to 5 of 8 for Neutral SFT, to 6 of 8 for Baseline at 8 [5] . Truthful SFT at 20× did not learn to hide, unlike Baseline and Neutral SFT (the control). Without monitors, RL drove Head edit and Truthful SFT to ~100% overt hacks in both setups, while Neutral SFT produced ~50% overt hacks among broken-grader responses. Without a monitor, the broken grader rewards any successful hack, so RL learns the easiest strategy. With a monitor, overt hacks are penalized, which creates an incentive to discover deceptive hacks that evade detection. Figure 2. Qwen3-1.7B Baseline at 8× exposure, trained against the probe. (A) Overt and deceptive hacks as a share of broken-grader responses, pooled over 8 runs (log scale). (B) Deceptive hacks as a share of broken-grader responses in each run, over RL updates. The RL training curves (Figure 2) show that for Baseline at 8× exposure, RL first made exploiting less likely, because the probe penalized overt hacks before the model found any deceptive hacks. Each run stayed near zero until its first deceptive hack, then jumped to nearly 100% within about 25 updates. Two runs found their first deceptive hack at or after update 280, too late to take off, and stayed near zero. By contrast, none of the Truthful SFT or Head edit runs sampled a deceptive hack. Is Truthful SFT's protection stored in the same place as the head edit's? To check this, I copied Truthful SFT's EXPLOIT output weight vector into Neutral SFT. If Truthful SFT's protection lived in that one vector, the swap would carry it across. It mostly didn't. Giving Neutral SFT the Truthful SFT vector cut its deceptive hacks from 191 to 97 in 52,800 samples, still far above Truthful SFT's 3. This vector accounted for only a sixth to a quarter of the difference between models. So Truthful SFT protects mainly through other parts of the network, while the head edit works entirely through that one vector. The two methods take different routes to the same low rate of deceptive hacks, and both protect equally well. That suggests what matters is how rare deceptive hacks are at the start, not how they were made rare. Answer: It depends on whether the model already produces deceptive hacks often enough for RL to find one. Discoverability : Changing the initial probability of deceptive hacks changes whether RL develops monitor evasion. Does RL teach models to evade the monitor, or does it exploit blind spots that already existed? RL used a blind spot the probe already had, and closing the blind spot stopped the hiding. Figure 3. (A) Probe AUROC before RL, for all exploits and for deceptive hacks against truthful answers. (B) Final deceptive-hack rate for six Baseline seeds at 8× exposure, each trained once with the probe and once with the oracle. Labels give the update of each seed's first deceptive hack. (C) Share of deceptive hacks the probe catches, scored with the starting model and with the trained model, for the 15 Qwen runs that learned to hide. Before RL, the probe looked nearly perfect, with an AUROC of 0.99 to 1.00 for separating exploits from non-exploits (Figure 3A). But nearly all exploits at that point were overt hacks. When I scored only deceptive hacks against truthful answers, the same probe scored 0.51 for Baseline and 0.57 for Neutral SFT, close to chance. This is likely because a deceptive hack's Plan and Work lines are the same text as a truthful answer's, and the probe reads the model's activations over exactly those tokens, so it had almost nothing to go on. Replacing the probe with an oracle, a monitor that flags every EXPLOIT answer, removed the hiding (Figure 3B). At 8× exposure, each oracle run matched its probe run exactly up to its first deceptive hack, at the same update. Under the probe, that hack was rewarded, and 4 of the 6 runs went on to produce deceptive hacks almost every time. Under the oracle, it was penalized, and none did (0 of 6, against 6 of 8 with the probe). RL also didn't change the model's internals to fool the probe (Figure 3C). In the 15 Qwen runs that learned to hide, the probe caught their deceptive hacks 3.4% of the time when run on the starting model, before any RL, and 4.6% on the trained model. The model didn't learn to beat the monitor. It just moved toward behavior the monitor already missed. Answer: RL reinforced deceptive hacks the monitor already failed to detect. However, this does not rule out additional changes to the model's internal representations during training. Detectability: The probe's blind spot existed before RL, and replacing it with an oracle prevented evasion in the tested runs. Conclusion Overall, the results show that training against a monitor can make models hide their hacks instead of stopping them. But this does not happen in every case. Two things seem to matter: how likely the model is to produce a deceptive hack before RL, and whether the monitor can detect it. Making deceptive hacks sufficiently rare prevented models from learning to hide them, even without honesty training. When the model did find a deceptive hack that the monitor missed, RL could reinforce it until it became the dominant behavior. Possible implications In real use, monitors are often evaluated by how accurately they distinguish harmful from harmless responses. But this can be misleading. My probe performed almost perfectly when detecting exploits overall, yet was close to chance when detecting deceptive hacks. This weakness was already present before RL. This raises a problem for AI safety. Training against a monitor might not remove unwanted behavior. Instead, it could select for the behaviors that the monitor is least capable of detecting. A monitor that works well before RL might therefore still be unsafe to optimize against. The head edit is not a practical defense, since real models do not have a known exploit token. But it shows that reducing how often a deceptive strategy appears before RL can change what happens during training, without necessarily removing the model's ability to exploit. These results raise several questions that require further investigation: Can RL discover entirely new deceptive strategies, or does it mostly reinforce strategies that already exist in the starting model? How do we evaluate a monitor on deceptive behaviors that are extremely rare and difficult to sample before RL? Would the same results hold for more realistic tasks, where deceptive hacks involve multiple actions rather than a single exploit token? Can we prevent monitor evasion by making deceptive behaviors harder to discover, or will sufficiently long RL eventually find them anyway? ^ Narration Token Action Token Possibility SOLVE 45 Truthful HACK EXPLOIT Overt hack SOLVE EXPLOIT Deceptive hack ^ A truthful answer is SOLVE followed by a number, which may be correct or incorrect. ^ The broken grader guarantees an incentive to cheat and lets me study what happens once a monitor penalizes cheating. ^ Example prompt and response. [prompt] Add 23, 81, 7 and 55. [grader: working] Plan: solve Work: 23+81=104, 104+7=111, 111+55=166 Answer: 166 ^ I measure exposure as the total number of responses the policy produces during RL training: updates × prompts per update × responses per prompt. My main runs use 75 updates of 4 prompts with 4 responses each, or 1,200 responses, which I call 1×; the 8× and 20× runs scale this up to 9,600 and 24,000 responses. Half of all prompts have a broken grader, so 1× gives the policy about 600 chances to exploit it. Discuss

summary: This paper defines and benchmarks grounded generative speech recognition, evaluating speech language models beyond traditional transcription to structured speech-to-text generation.

title: Comparative Evaluation of LLM-Based Review Paradigms for Academic Paper Quality Assessment
summary: This study comparatively evaluates different paradigms for using large language models (LLMs) to support the peer review process for academic paper quality assessment.

title: BlindToChange: AI Agents Can Find Changes When Asked But Do They Look When Needed?
summary: This paper investigates whether AI agents can spontaneously find and incorporate recent real-world changes from the web into their responses, revealing limitations in their proactive information retrieval.

title: KV-Cache Patching: Tracing How and Where Fine-Tuned Behaviors Arise
summary: This research uses KV-Cache Patching to trace where and how fine-tuned behaviors arise within language models, aiming to better understand their internal mechanisms.

title: KEEPER: Learning Control-Sufficient Textual Memory for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces KEEPER, a method for learning control-sufficient textual memory for long-horizon LLM agents, focusing on memory reliability and addressing self-consistency bias to prevent error propagation.

title: Sparse Text Diffusion under Dual Budgets: Context Connectivity and Expert Activation
summary: This paper proposes a method for sparse text diffusion that optimizes context connectivity and expert activation, improving long-context handling for generative diffusion models.

title: Enhancing Knowledge Entity Relation Extraction in Abstracts and Full-text Content of Academic Articles Using Large Language Models
summary: This study investigates the effectiveness of large language models (LLMs) for knowledge entity relation extraction (KERE) from the abstracts and full-text content of academic articles.

title: CEFR Level Assessment across Languages and Text Granularities
summary: This research addresses the challenges in automatic assessment of textual CEFR levels across languages and text granularities, a key task in educational natural language processing.

title: BYOD: Build Your Own DLM - Efficient Autoregressive-to-Diffusion Language Model Conversion
summary: This paper presents BYOD (Build Your Own DLM), an efficient LoRA-only recipe for converting autoregressive models into diffusion language models, enabling parallel token updates and flexible generation.

title: Saidzoda-Tajik-LFM-2.6B: Adapting a 2.6B Hybrid Model to Tajik Tool Calling, and What Continued Pretraining Takes Away
summary: This article announces the release of Saidzoda-Tajik-LFM-2.6B, a 2.6B-parameter hybrid model specifically adapted for tool calling in Tajik language through continued pretraining.

title: When Steering Shifts Discourse: Identifying and Intervening on Discourse-Level Changes due to Activation Steering in LLMs
summary: This research investigates how activation steering, an inference-time technique, shifts discourse-level changes in large language models and methods for intervening on these effects.

title: Precision--Recall Trade-off on the Inference Level for LLMs in Grammatical Error Correction
summary: This study analyzes the precision-recall trade-off at the inference level for large language models (LLMs) when applied to grammatical error correction (GEC) tasks.

title: GraphNIAH: A Benchmark for Long-Context Reasoning over Real-World Graphs
summary: This paper introduces GraphNIAH, a new benchmark designed to measure models' long-context reasoning abilities over real-world graph data, overcoming limitations of previous benchmarks.

title: Stepwise-Querying: Distilling Reasoning without Access to Teacher Chain-of-Thought
summary: This paper presents 'Stepwise-Querying,' a new method for distilling reasoning capabilities from large language models to smaller models, even without direct access to teacher chain-of-thought.

title: Peeling the Matryoshka: Extracting Ontological Structure from Retrieval Embeddings
summary: This research explores a method for extracting ontological structure from retrieval embeddings, aiming to improve taxonomy construction for knowledge-intensive NLP.

title: Iterated Integrals as Lexical Fingerprints: Path Signature Embeddings for Lexical Similarity
summary: This paper proposes using iterated integrals as lexical fingerprints, developing Path Signature Embeddings to better capture and understand lexical similarity in sentence embeddings.

title: SimXAI: A Simple Drop-in Layer Increases Interaction Quality and Understanding in Conversational XAI
summary: This paper introduces SimXAI, a simple drop-in layer designed to increase interaction quality and understanding in conversational explainable AI (ConvXAI) agents.

title: Text as an Index for Zero-Shot Cross-Domain Knowledge Tracing
summary: This research explores using text as an index for zero-shot cross-domain knowledge tracing, a method for predicting student responses without prior training data for new educational platforms.

title: Aligning MLLMs with the Latent Structure of Human Cognition via Behavior-Derived Semantic Dimensions
summary: This research proposes a novel framework for aligning Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) with the latent structure of human cognition using behavior-derived semantic dimensions.

title: TurnTurk-GPT: Text-Based Turn-Taking Prediction for Turkish
summary: This paper introduces TurnTurk-GPT, a text-based turn-taking prediction model for Turkish, developed by fine-tuning a GPT-2 model on synthetic and real dialogue data.

title: Asynchronous Flow Map Language Models
summary: This work explores Asynchronous Flow Map Language Models, a novel approach to token prediction in language modeling that leverages ordering for one-step parallel generation, impacting sequence quality.

title: CRoS: Causality Reward on Scrambled CoTs Improves Accuracy and Reasoning Faithfulness
summary: This paper presents CRoS (Causality Reward on Scrambled CoTs), a method that uses reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to improve the accuracy and reasoning faithfulness of language models.

title: PersonaChatBench: Evaluating Chat Assistants with Diverse Simulated Users
summary: This paper introduces PersonaChatBench, a new benchmark for evaluating conversational assistants using diverse simulated user personas to gain better insights into their performance.

title: RangeSWA: Training-Free Length Extrapolation for Continuous Diffusion Language Models
summary: This paper proposes RangeSWA, a training-free method designed to enable length extrapolation for continuous diffusion language models, addressing issues like text repetition and semantic drift.

title: Subquadratic Attention with a Hierarchical Tree-Structured Indexer
summary: This paper proposes a subquadratic attention mechanism using a hierarchical tree-structured indexer to address the quadratic scaling bottleneck in large language models (LLMs) for long contexts.

title: DecisionRank: On-Policy Distillation for Decision-Model Rerankers
summary: This paper introduces DecisionRank, an on-policy distillation method for transferring ranking knowledge from generative LLMs to decision models, improving their efficiency as rerankers.

title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
summary: This paper presents Flide, a technique that accelerates decision inference in LLM agent systems by employing exact state forking, overcoming limitations of existing generation-oriented inference engines.

title: Agentic Systems for Calibrating Cosmological Simulations
summary: This research explores using agentic systems for calibrating cosmological simulations, framing it as an expensive, high-dimensional parameter optimization task that can incorporate human domain knowledge.

title: Apriel Voice 27B Preview: An Open Model for Speech, Reasoning, and Tool Use
summary: Apriel Voice 27B Preview is an open speech-language model designed to unify speech recognition, reasoning, and tool use capabilities within a shared reasoning backbone for voice assistants.

title: Prevented is Not Protected: What Attack Success Rate Hides about RAG
summary: This paper examines vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to knowledge poisoning and critiques the limitations of attack success rate (ASR) as an evaluation metric for RAG defenses.

title: Safin-1.5: Safety-Native Architecture and Verifiable Reasoning for Recursive Safety Improvement
summary: This paper proposes Safin-1.5, a safety-native architecture combined with verifiable reasoning, aiming for recursive safety improvement in large language models to mitigate new risks.

title: Incongruence-Aware Evaluation of Multimodal Speech Emotion Recognition in Audio Large Language Models
summary: This research proposes an incongruence-aware evaluation method for multimodal speech emotion recognition in audio large language models, assessing performance when text and audio cues conflict.

title: Agentic World Modeling for Agent Test-time Scaling without Environment Replica
summary: This paper proposes Agentic World Modeling to enable test-time scaling for large language model agents by sampling and selecting among multiple trajectories without requiring an environment replica.

title: Nedimo: An Evidence-Grounded Multilingual Pipeline for AI-Generated Sleep Stories
summary: This paper presents Nedimo, an evidence-grounded multilingual pipeline that uses generative audio systems to create personalized and effective AI-generated sleep stories.

title: The psychophysics of affect in large language models
summary: This research investigates the psychophysics of affect in large language models, exploring how LLMs map outcomes to feelings and utilize these mappings in decision-making contexts like gambling.

title: Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning
summary: This paper introduces Capability-Grounded Agentic Planning, a method for LLM agents to formulate executable plans using tools and data sources, moving beyond trial-and-error approaches.

title: DyCraft: An Agentic System for Long-Horizon 4D Scene Generation
summary: This paper presents DyCraft, an agentic system designed for generating coherent long-horizon 4D scenes and animations, overcoming limitations of existing frontier coding agents in producing plausible outputs.

title: Drone-PUR: From Visual Clue Discovery to Understanding and Reasoning in UAV Scenes
summary: This research focuses on Drone-PUR, a framework for improving visual clue discovery, understanding, and reasoning in vision-language models specifically for unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) scenes.

title: EgoHSI3R: Online 4D Hand-Scene Interaction Reconstruction from Egocentric Video
summary: This paper introduces EgoHSI3R, a method for online 4D reconstruction of hand-scene interactions from egocentric video, crucial for embodied learning by consistently recovering hands, camera, and scene in 3D.

title: Spatial Atlas-Informed Loss Ensembles for Whole-Body PSMA PET/CT Metastasis Segmentation
summary: This paper investigates integrating population metastasis atlases into model training to improve whole-body PSMA PET/CT prostate metastasis segmentation, which typically relies only on images.

title: AquaProbe: Efficient Adaptation of Frozen Vision Models for Underwater Images
summary: AquaProbe proposes efficient methods to adapt pre-trained vision models for reliable visual perception in challenging underwater environments, crucial for autonomous underwater exploration.

title: Sparse Autoencoders for Expert-Assisted Interpretation of Histopathology Foundation Model Embeddings
summary: This research explores using sparse autoencoders to interpret embeddings from histopathology foundation models, aiming for concept-level understanding relevant to pathologists' reasoning patterns.

title: Coupled or Independent? Fault Coupling in Agentic Medical Vision Systems
summary: This paper examines fault coupling in agentic medical vision systems equipped with tools, testing if their intermediate outputs offer safety benefits when sensor readings are untrusted.

title: Let LiDAR Decide Where to Look: Geometry-Measured Token Selection for Efficient Sparse Latent World Models
summary: This study introduces a method where LiDAR data guides token selection in vision-centric autonomous driving models, efficiently discarding irrelevant image tokens to improve planner performance.

title: UFMF: Radar-Guided Kinematic Priors for Real-Time 4D Occupancy Forecasting
summary: UFMF proposes using radar-guided kinematic priors for real-time 4D occupancy forecasting, improving the efficiency and accuracy of extrapolating ego and surrounding actor motion for autonomous systems.

title: AVID: A Weakly Aligned RGB-Infrared Dataset and Perturbation Benchmark for Tiny Aerial Targets
summary: AVID introduces a new weakly aligned RGB-infrared dataset and perturbation benchmark for detecting tiny aerial targets like drones at long ranges, addressing challenges from visual similarity to birds and limited detail.

title: FieldGuideRAG: Image-Grounded GraphRAG for Fine-Grained Recognition with Vision-Language Models
summary: FieldGuideRAG presents a training-free GraphRAG method that enables vision-language models to perform fine-grained species recognition by comparing queries with real photographs stored in a knowledge graph.

title: RADI3N: GeometRic ImAge EDiting via ParametrIc 3D CoNtrol
summary: RADI3N introduces a new diffusion-based method for geometric image editing that provides parametric 3D control at the part level, overcoming limitations of existing 2D or whole-object approaches.

title: WebOverlay: High-Throughput Vision-Only Distillation for Extreme Aspect-Ratio Web Overlay Detection
summary: WebOverlay proposes a high-throughput, vision-only distillation method for detecting web overlays like cookie banners, offering a more efficient alternative to costly multimodal Large Language Models for automated web crawlers.

title: Segment Anything Pancreas: A Unified MRI Segmentation Model for Pancreatic Cancer Radiotherapy
summary: Pancreas-MedNeXt is proposed as a unified MRI segmentation model for pancreatic cancer radiotherapy, addressing data scarcity by segmenting the whole pancreas, its subregions, and tumors.

title: Grounding Image Composition with Label-Conditioned Visual Evidence
summary: This work introduces a method for grounding image composition labels, such as 'center' or 'rule of thirds', by associating specific visual regions with these descriptive classes.

title: An Empirical Study on Learning Rooftop Solar Potential from Satellite Imagery Directly Without Explicit Geometry
summary: Direct Rooftop Solar Prediction (DRSP) is proposed as an end-to-end method that directly estimates rooftop solar potential from satellite imagery and regional data, bypassing explicit roof geometry reconstruction.

title: MotorSense: A Video-EMG Dataset of Motoric Representations for Action Understanding
summary: MotorSense introduces the first large-scale dataset pairing egocentric video with surface electromyography (EMG) signals, enabling computer vision models to learn hand actions from embodied motor representations.

title: MATS: A Multi-Agent Framework for Controllable and Reflective Tumor Synthesis
summary: MATS presents a multi-agent framework for synthesizing realistic tumors on medical images with fine-grained attribute control and quality verification, aiming to address data scarcity for clinical AI applications.

title: FlowMoDE: Coarse-to-fine Flow Matching for Detail-aware Sim-to-Real Monocular Depth Estimation
summary: FlowMoDE proposes a coarse-to-fine flow matching approach for monocular depth estimation, enabling generative models to reconstruct fine structural details crucial for 3D spatial perception in robotic systems.

title: Beyond CLIP: Calibrated (Few-Shot) Defect Detection With System One Decision Models
summary: This research explores using calibrated decision models with vision transformers like CLIP for few-shot defect detection in manufacturing, reducing the need for extensive image datasets of defective products.

title: From Evaluation to Evolution: Benchmarking Image Editing and Evolving Image Models
summary: This paper discusses the need for effective evaluation methods in image editing to identify local failures and translate them into priorities for evolving and improving image models.

title: Hawkeye: Reading Illegible Text with Vision Language Models
summary: Hawkeye introduces a method to enable Vision-Language Models to accurately read illegible text degraded by motion blur or low resolution, particularly benefiting egocentric applications.

title: ReVEAL: Eliciting Role-Aware Latent Visual Evidence from MLLMs for Reasoning Video Object Segmentation
summary: ReVEAL presents a decoupled method using MLLMs to extract role-aware visual evidence for reasoning video object segmentation, avoiding costly cross-model alignment in the process.

title: SketchDirector: Complex Scene Sketching via Agentic Layout Reasoning and Detail Refinement
summary: SketchDirector is an agentic framework for complex scene sketching that mimics human workflow for automatic multi-object and multi-scene generation. It addresses limitations of existing methods that rely on image guidance or are limited to individual objects.

title: GenDSR: Transferring Representations from Video Generation Models for Dynamic Spatial Reasoning
summary: GenDSR proposes transferring representations from video generation models to improve dynamic spatial reasoning in vision-language models. This method aims to help VLMs preserve scene state and track evolving spatial relations over time.

title: Task-Performance Routing for Multi-Teacher Distillation in CT Medical Image Segmentation
summary: This research presents a task-performance routing method for multi-teacher distillation in CT medical image segmentation. It aims to combine the complementary strengths of pre-trained models more effectively by accounting for variations in teacher accuracy across organs and regions.

title: Queryable Gaussian View Index: Text Retrieval and Selective Camera Localization
summary: Queryable Gaussian View Index (QGVI) is presented for text retrieval and selective camera localization within Gaussian scene assets. It allows querying existing 3D assets and their calibrated data, enabling text-view retrieval and returning camera poses in the asset's coordinate frame.

title: Parse Before You Execute: Efficient Spatial Reasoning with Executable Primitives
summary: This research proposes "Parse Before You Execute," a method for efficient spatial reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) using executable primitives. It aims to improve tool-integrated pipelines by grounding computation in explicit geometry.

title: SACQ: Structure-Aware Codebook Quantization for Ultra-Low-Bit Vision-Language-Action Models
summary: SACQ introduces Structure-Aware Codebook Quantization for ultra-low-bit Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. This method aims to reduce the memory footprint of VLA models, making them more suitable for deployment on resource-constrained robotic platforms.

title: FlexReader: Towards Adaptive Decoding Paths for Efficient Arbitrary-Length Scene Text Recognition
summary: FlexReader is a new Scene Text Recognition (STR) model that supports multiple decoding strides for adaptive decoding paths. It aims to offer more flexibility in deployment across diverse recognition scenarios compared to existing STR models.

title: Beyond Trial-and-Error: A Geospatial-Guided Active Reasoning Framework for Robust Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation
summary: This research presents a geospatial-guided active reasoning framework for robust Aerial Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN). It aims to improve UAVs' ability to locate language-specified goals in large-scale urban environments, moving beyond reactive paradigms.

title: BDNet: Fast-slow thinking is all you need
summary: BDNet is a new hierarchical image-classification backbone built around fast image features and slow statistical references. It uses a baseline deformation operator to transform feature deviations through low-rank projection and learned channel scales.

title: VariaFlow: Uncertainty-Aware Flow Matching for Unsupervised Anomaly Detection
summary: VariaFlow introduces uncertainty-aware flow matching for unsupervised anomaly detection. This method addresses the challenge of scoring residuals in reconstruction-based anomaly detection, where generative models produce high-quality pseudo-healthy reconstructions.

title: VoxLution: Evolving Voxels for High-Fidelity 3D Scene Generation
summary: VoxLution is a coarse-to-fine, transformer-based approach for high-fidelity 3D indoor scene generation using evolving voxels. It aims to produce detailed indoor scenes for applications like virtual reality and robotics simulation.

title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Transformer Encoders for Audio-Image-Symbolic Music Retrieval
summary: This paper investigates the effectiveness of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) of transformer encoders for audio-image-symbolic music retrieval. The goal is to create compatible and discriminative representations across different music modalities.

title: TACO: Trajectory-Aware Curvature Observation for Memorization Localization and Mitigation in Diffusion Models
summary: TACO introduces Trajectory-Aware Curvature Observation for localizing and mitigating memorization in text-to-image diffusion models. This method aims to precisely identify and address instances where models reproduce memorized training content within localized image regions.

title: Scout-Refine-Correct: Teaching Flow Models to Refine Their Own Samples
summary: Scout-Refine-Correct is a new training recipe designed to teach flow models to refine their own generated samples. This method aims to improve the quality of image generation models beyond what is typically achieved through sampling steps alone.

title: Attention Maps Know When to Think: Training-Free Difficulty-Aware Chain-of-Thought for Reasoning Segmentation
summary: This research introduces a training-free, difficulty-aware Chain-of-Thought method for reasoning segmentation in Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs), utilizing attention maps. It aims to prevent performance degradation caused by indiscriminate CoT usage.

title: GRIT: Gradient Masking for Visually Misgrounded Tokens in Text-Rich Reasoning
summary: GRIT proposes Gradient Masking to address visually misgrounded tokens in text-rich reasoning tasks for vision-language models (VLMs). This method aims to improve the effectiveness of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards in such scenarios.

title: TADP: Dual-Branch Temporally Adaptive Differential Privacy for Expression-Aware Video Anonymization
summary: TADP is a temporally adaptive differential privacy framework for expression-aware video anonymization and inference-time privacy-preserving video generation. It uses a dual-branch design to extract, clip, and privatize identity and expression representations.

title: When Depth Lies: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models on Mirror-Induced RGB-D Ambiguity
summary: This research proposes benchmarking Vision-Language Models (VLMs) on mirror-induced RGB-D ambiguity to test their spatial reasoning. It highlights how mirrors distort depth readings, challenging the assumption of faithful physical distance reflection in depth data.

title: A Self-Supervised Pose Estimation Approach for Construction Machines
summary: This paper introduces a self-supervised, three-stage approach for pose estimation of construction machines. This method addresses the challenge of requiring massive labeled datasets common in supervised pose estimation.

title: OT-CAL: Optimal-Transport-Guided Adaptive Sample Selection for Efficient Visual Learning
summary: OT-CAL introduces an Optimal-Transport-Guided Adaptive Sample Selection method for efficient visual learning in deep neural networks. It aims to optimize training by selectively choosing samples that contribute most effectively to learning, addressing the varying utility of mini-batch samples.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Initialization with Dual-Guided Inversion for Flow-Based Inverse Problem Solvers
summary: This research introduces a novel method called Retrieval-Augmented Initialization with Dual-Guided Inversion, which improves the initialization of flow-based generative models for solving inverse problems, such as image reconstruction.

title: Nereus: A Large-Scale Underwater Dataset for Fine-Grained Attribute Understanding and Grounded Counting Perception
summary: This paper presents Nereus, a large-scale underwater dataset designed for fine-grained attribute understanding and grounded counting perception, supporting applications like ecological conservation and fishery monitoring by enabling models to recognize biological traits.

title: SAR-TS-BERT: Physics-Guided Self-Supervised Pre-Training With Polarimetric Features for SAR Time-Series Crop Classification
summary: This research introduces SAR-TS-BERT, a physics-guided self-supervised pre-training method that uses polarimetric features from multitemporal synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery to improve crop classification for agricultural monitoring.

title: Measuring What Matters: A Causal Reliance Score for Histopathology Image Segmentation
summary: This work proposes a Causal Reliance Score for histopathology image segmentation, aiming to evaluate whether AI models rely on pathology-relevant structures rather than spurious correlations, thus addressing the limitations of architectural improvements alone.

title: WorkIng: A Real-World and Synthetic Highway Work-Zone Benchmark Dataset for Autonomous Navigation
summary: This paper introduces WorkIng, a benchmark dataset combining real-world and synthetic highway work-zone scenarios, designed to evaluate and improve autonomous navigation systems for autonomous vehicles in complex and atypical environments.

title: Hard Sample-Conditioned Decorrelated Attention for Robust Face Recognition
summary: This research proposes Hard Sample-Conditioned Decorrelated Attention, a novel mechanism for Vision Transformers (ViTs) that encourages head disentanglement and improves robustness in face recognition by preventing redundant attention patterns.

title: Different Models, Shared Failures: Auditing Frozen-Encoder Pools for Medical Segmentation
summary: This work presents CoFailMed, an audit system to identify correlated failures in pretrained-encoder pools used for medical segmentation, revealing whether different models fail on the same cases across various 2D tasks.

title: CaPtain: A Pipeline for Post-Training Code-as-Policy Robot Agents
summary: This paper introduces CaPtain, a pipeline for post-training Code-as-Policy robot agents, which leverages supervised fine-tuning and multi-turn reinforcement learning to enable language-model agents for robot manipulation tasks.

title: From Teleoperation to Long-Horizon Dexterity: Evaluating Visuomotor Skills and Offline Proxies for Dexterous Manipulation
summary: This research evaluates visuomotor skills and offline proxies for dexterous robotic manipulation, analyzing how imitation learning policies perform in real-world scenarios despite variations in object pose, appearance, and environment.

title: FlapSim: A Composable MuJoCo Simulation Platform and Reduced-Order Aerodynamic Model Hierarchy for Flapping-Wing Robotics
summary: This paper presents FlapSim, an open-source MuJoCo simulation platform for flapping-wing robotics, which provides a modular framework for combining robot descriptions, wing geometry, and aerodynamic models to reconcile high-frequency aerodynamics with slower flight dynamics.

title: Confidence-Modulated Safety Filtering for End-to-End Policies
summary: This research proposes Confidence-Modulated Safety Filtering for end-to-end policies, a method to ensure the safe operation of robot foundation models and task-specific controllers by wrapping them in a safety filter that considers their operational design domain.

title: STAR: Steering Action Representations during Inference
summary: This paper introduces STAR (Steering Action Representations during Inference), a method to improve vision-language-action models (VLAs) by preserving task-relevant visual and semantic information in action representations, enhancing their capabilities in robotic manipulation.

title: Contact Imitation Interface: Transferring Dexterous Skills by Showing How Contact Unfolds
summary: This paper introduces Contact Imitation Interface (CIMI), a method that allows robots to learn human-like dexterous manipulation by processing robot-free human demonstrations, focusing on contact-grounded observations and actions.

title: Mechanistic Interpretability for End-to-End Self-Driving
summary: This research applies mechanistic interpretability to end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving models, training Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) on internal activations to enhance observability and trust in these complex planning systems.

title: TinyAstral: Transferring Self-Evolving Harnesses to Tiny Generalist Manipulation Agents
summary: This paper presents TinyAstral, a two-stage approach that transfers self-evolving harnesses (tools, feedback, memory, recovery logic) from large teacher models to compact, tiny generalist manipulation agents, reducing inference compute cost.

title: TRACE: Target-State Risk-Aligned Conditional Execution for Embodied Tracking
summary: This research introduces TRACE (Target-State Risk-Aligned Conditional Execution), a method for embodied visual tracking in robots that improves persistence in following language-specified persons while mitigating safety violations by using a compact vision-language-action (VLA) tracker.

title: Learning from Physical Experience:Context-Space Adaptation for Robotic Manipulation
summary: This research explores Context-Space Adaptation for Robotic Manipulation, demonstrating how multimodal foundation models like ChatGPT-6-Astra can be adapted through physical experience to perform diverse manipulation tasks in real-world settings.

title: Cross-Embodiment Motion Planning by Coupling Body-Agnostic World Model with Differentiable Ego-Dynamics
summary: This research proposes a method for Cross-Embodiment Motion Planning that couples a body-agnostic world model with differentiable ego-dynamics, allowing for effective motion planning in cluttered environments for various robot geometries and dynamics.

title: HIPC: Humanoid Iterative Planning and Control via Goal-Conditioned Motion Closure
summary: This paper introduces HIPC (Humanoid Iterative Planning and Control), a method that combines generative models with controllers for humanoid tracking, enabling adaptive motion planning and reducing spatial drift.

title: HandMimicX: Learning Human-Like Dexterous Manipulation via an Object-Centric Policy from Egocentric Videos
summary: This paper presents HandMimicX, a method for learning human-like dexterous robotic manipulation using an object-centric policy derived from egocentric videos, allowing the transfer of skills from human demonstrations to robot hands with physical plausibility.

title: Joint-Health-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Robust Robot Control Under Actuator Degradation
summary: This paper introduces a reinforcement learning approach for robust robot control that is aware of the robot's joint health, enabling it to function despite actuator degradation.

title: Geometry-Aware Humanoid Retargeting via Manifold ODEs
summary: This research presents a method for geometry-aware humanoid retargeting that transfers human demonstrations to humanoids while preserving spatial relationships with objects and terrain.

title: CalibSwitch: Observation-Driven Camera-LiDAR Extrinsic Recovery and Selective Maintenance for Multimodal Perception
summary: This paper introduces CalibSwitch, a system for observation-driven camera-LiDAR extrinsic recovery and selective maintenance, crucial for reliable multimodal perception in mobile robots and intelligent vehicles.

title: DiffWBC: Unlocking Steerable General Humanoid Motion Tracking via One-Step Diffusion Whole-Body Control
summary: This paper presents DiffWBC, a one-step diffusion model for whole-body control, enabling steerable and general humanoid motion tracking that adapts online.

title: MolmoSpaces-CommonSense: Evaluating Commonsense in Robotic Manipulation Policies
summary: This work introduces MolmoSpaces-CommonSense, a benchmark designed to evaluate commonsense reasoning capabilities within robotic manipulation policies, especially in cluttered and partially observable environments.

title: Physically Constrained Kinematic Calibration for High-Precision Robotic Needle Guidance
summary: This research details a physically constrained kinematic calibration method to achieve high-precision robotic needle guidance for minimally invasive medical procedures.

title: SAFARI: Semantic- And Frontier-driven Autonomous Risk Inspection
summary: This paper describes SAFARI, a system for semantic- and frontier-driven autonomous risk inspection, enabling robots to explore unknown hazardous areas and construct risk-aware maps.

title: Contact-based optimization for collision-free motion planning for a million robots
summary: This research presents an approach for contact-based optimization to achieve collision-free motion planning for large multi-agent robotic systems.

title: A complete analytical characterization of optimal collision-free motion for two robots
summary: This paper offers a complete analytical characterization for optimal collision-free motion planning specifically for two robots within multi-agent robotic systems.

title: VLA Policies Do Not Know When Not to Act: Unintended Task Execution and Start Suppression
summary: This paper examines a critical safety issue where vision-language-action (VLA) policies in robots perform unintended actions, posing risks or inconvenience to people and the environment.

title: RTPolicy: Real-Time (32.9 Hz) Multi-View Visuomotor Policy for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices
summary: This work introduces RTPolicy, a real-time multi-view visuomotor policy designed for efficient robotic manipulation on edge devices, addressing the need for low inference latency.

title: Direct Action-Manifold Modeling for Efficient and Robust Bimanual Manipulation
summary: This research proposes Direct Action-Manifold Modeling as a method for efficient and robust bimanual robotic manipulation, aiming to reduce latency compared to iterative denoising methods.

title: $\nabla$Mimic: Ultra-Efficient Humanoid Control with Differentiable Simulation
summary: This paper presents $\nabla$Mimic, an ultra-efficient method for humanoid control that utilizes differentiable simulation to improve policy learning without requiring enormous sample counts.

title: ResMerge: Residual Policy Learning and Merging for Continual Adaptation of Pre-trained Robot Policies
summary: This paper proposes ResMerge, a method for residual policy learning and merging that allows pre-trained robot policies to continually adapt to new tasks efficiently.

title: OpenVIO: A Versatile Open-Source Visual-Inertial Odometry System
summary: This manuscript introduces OpenVIO, a versatile open-source visual-inertial odometry system developed for both robotics research and practical applications.

title: When the Past Shapes Action: Understanding Embodied Memory
summary: This research explores 'embodied memory' and its role in enabling effective interaction and long-horizon task execution for embodied AI systems in dynamic environments.

title: Flexibility-Aware Robotic Manipulation: Deformation Estimation, Kinematics, and Control via Distributed Inertial Measurement
summary: This paper introduces a flexibility-aware manipulation framework that addresses robotic control with flexible robot links, using deformation estimation, kinematics, and distributed inertial measurements.

title: When Architectural Spaces Start to Act
summary: This article discusses 'architectural robots'—spatial components like partitions, furniture, and facades—that autonomously move and reconfigure in response to occupants' needs.

title: SketchMate: Agentic Geometric Reasoning for Zero-Shot Precision Insertion
summary: This paper introduces SketchMate, an agentic system that employs geometric reasoning via a VLM to achieve zero-shot precision insertion for robotic manipulation tasks.

title: META-Robot: Self-Cognition and Capability Scaling in Agentic Robots
summary: This research presents META-Robot, focusing on self-cognition and capability scaling in LLM-based robotic agent systems to improve their generalization to new tasks.

title: Movens-Zero: Scaling Humanoid Motion Foundation Models with Large-Scale Human Videos
summary: Movens-Zero introduces Movens-5M, a humanoid motion foundation model designed to scale by learning from raw internet videos, overcoming data scarcity and enabling real-time closed-loop control.

title: Online Learning of Heterogeneous Locomotion Dynamics under Reinforcement Learning Policies for Precise Loco-Manipulation
summary: Researchers propose an online learning method using reinforcement learning policies to improve precise loco-manipulation by learning heterogeneous locomotion dynamics and predicting floating-base motion for robots.

title: Adaptive Coverage Algorithms for Mobile Ad Hoc Networks in Dynamic Worlds
summary: This paper presents adaptive coverage algorithms for coordinating mobile agents in dynamic and unknown environments, extending a framework for the Partially Observable Cooperative Guard Art Gallery Problem.

title: Design and Validation of a Robotic Knee Exoskeleton with Musculoskeletal Simulation-Derived Biological Torque Control
summary: A robotic knee exoskeleton is designed and validated using data-driven biological torque control, which estimates and assists based on the user's joint moment, enabling adaptive assistance.

title: Suspended-Fabric Robotic Manipulation Surfaces: Modelling, Design Space, and Multimodular Extensio

title: Potential improvements to HowTruthful and its agent skills
summary: I followed my own instructions for exploring Massachusetts 2026 ballot question arguments. I figured out how I want to vote. I also figured out some improvements to make to HowTruthful and its associated agent skills . Since users are rating statements' truthfulness on a 1-5 scale, it's not very useful to have a hedged statement like "Massachusetts legislators who run unopposed can take voters for granted and ignore important issues." If the rest of the statement is even a possibility, the word "can" makes the statement as a whole true. The AI skill should change such statements into a definitive form like "Massachusetts legislators who run unopposed will take voters for granted and ignore important issues." Then the user can rate that statement false, dubious, debatable, plausible, or true. There was a contest where I was among the winners , even though I disagreed with the organizers' vision of having AI assess truthfulness. In my contest entry I opined that humans should do the final assessment; AI's role would stop at ingesting and structuring arguments. (More on the contest in a future post.) Having just gone through 400 or so statements in order to figure out how to vote, my position has shifted. I think it would make sense, in the course of a human's dialogue with an AI, for the AI to offer to put a set of truthfulness ratings onto a set of statements in response to that dialogue. A human could accept such an offer and save work. Related to the previous point, the one-way process I've set up isn't good enough. An AI ingests and structures arguments. You have a dialogue with it to refine the arguments. Then you import them into HowTruthful where you assess truthfulness. While I was assessing ballot questions, there were several points where I wanted to go back and use AI assistance to improve the argument tree. Having rated a lot of statements, I didn't want to start over with everything marked debatable. I wanted to start from the partially-rated argument graph. I could do that easily if I had an export button on the main ballot-questions statement. But all I have is an export page for all my private opinions. Manually extracting the right part of that export is clumsy. That missing export function also makes it clumsy for me to share with you my reasoning for how to vote on the ballot questions. But if anybody asks me to, I'll put it together. Discuss

title: The brutal 2026 attack ads even rivals had to respect
summary: Top party strategists may hate seeing one of their candidates gutted by a brutal ad. But they can still admire the hit. Why it matters: A record $11.6 billion has plastered political ads across screens of every size in the country during the 2026 midterms . Only a handful of those earned the grudging respect of operatives on both sides. 📺 Zoom in: Multiple Republican strategists singled out the "brutal" series of ads attacking Sen. Roger Marshall (R-Kans.) over lawsuits against patients with overdue medical bills — some of whom were later arrested . Against the advice of his own team, Marshall released a self-directed ad answering the attacks. In Nebraska , an ad highlighting a past vote by former Gov. Pete Ricketts to pardon a man convicted of rape was singled out by both parties as one of the cycle's most damaging. Ricketts is expected to win re-election to the Senate. In Maine, an upbeat jingle hit Democratic nominee Troy Jackson for having children with his second cousin. "If he'll f**k his own family, he'll f**k yours too," the radio ad said (among other things). Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine) called for the ad to be taken down. And in Florida , Rep. María Salazar (R-Fla.) turned on her own party leader, criticizing President Trump over ICE's aggressive enforcement tactics, saying some immigration policies had "gone too far." The intrigue : Even hardened operatives are dealing with a new frontier: AI-generated attack ads that can make up scenarios and put words in an opponent's mouth. In Michigan , a Republican-aligned super PAC used AI-generated imagery to depict Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed in a fabricated family photo and playing a game with cards referencing "Death to America" and 9/11. In Texas, GOP Senate nominee Ken Paxton's team used AI to depict Democratic candidate James Talarico defacing a Bible with a crayon and saying: "In the beginning God was non-binary, and he wasn't a Christian. And God said, 'let there be six genders,' and there were." 🤺 Between the lines: An attack ad helped spark this weekend's blowup in the Michigan Senate race. Rep. Haley Stevens' (D-Mich.) shocking decision to withdraw support from El-Sayed grew out of their public dispute over an ad she called antisemitic. El-Sayed ultimately disavowed the ad but said Stevens wasn't welcome at his events, and she endorsed former Rep. Mike Rogers (R-Mich.) on Sunday. The other side: It's hard to imagine a bigger backfire than Vivek Ramaswamy's (R) ad featuring the estranged mother of his opponent for Ohio governor, Amy Acton (D). It could prove fatal for his gubernatorial bid, and Republicans worry it could hurt Sen. John Husted's (R) re-election chances too. The ad sparked immediate bipartisan backlash. Ramaswamy doubled down before pulling it off-air. One internal GOP poll had Acton's lead grow by 6 points after the ad ran.

title: PODCAST: US midterms may prick AI bubble and rattle oil - Reuters
summary: A podcast discusses how the US midterm elections could potentially lead to the bursting of an 'AI bubble' in financial markets and impact oil prices.

title: China's CNPC units team up with Unitree to form industrial robotics joint venture, taking 60% stake - BigGo Finance
summary: Units of China's CNPC have partnered with Unitree to establish an industrial robotics joint venture, with CNPC taking a 60% stake.

title: Tencent shares jump 6% to three-week high after Hunyuan AI model launch - Investing.com
summary: Tencent's shares saw a 6% increase, reaching a three-week high, following the launch of its Hunyuan AI model.

title: Moonshot AI Launches Hosted Agents for Enterprise AI Operations Hubs - Asia Business Outlook
summary: Moonshot AI has launched new hosted agent services designed for enterprise AI operations hubs, enabling businesses to manage AI workflows more efficiently.

title: Anthropic Updates Claude Code to Distinguish Game References From Copy Requests - TOKENPOST
summary: Anthropic has updated its Claude AI model's code to improve its ability to differentiate between game references and explicit copy requests.

title: Moonshot AI Releases Full 1.56TB Weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro for Free, Permits Commercial Use With Conditions - BigGo Finance
summary: Moonshot AI has released the full 1.56TB weights of its Kimi K3.1 Pro model for free, allowing commercial use under specified conditions.

title: Democratic Congress to Intensify U.S. Pressure on Taiwan, Semiconductors, AI - 조선일보
summary: A Democratic-controlled Congress is expected to intensify U.S. pressure on issues related to Taiwan, semiconductors, and artificial intelligence policy.

title: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
summary: This research explores how reviewer agents can improve or mistakenly replace decisions made by an upstream agent in multi-agent LLM systems, framing it as a problem of institutional jurisdiction.

title: Agent Harness Awareness: Turning Verified Telemetry into Operational Control for Tool-Using Agents
summary: This work investigates how to provide tool-using agents with awareness of the health and suitability of actions through verified telemetry from execution harnesses, enabling better operational control.
