title: Uncertainty-Aware Resource Orchestration for Agentic AI Systems
summary: This research focuses on uncertainty-aware resource orchestration for agentic AI systems, which operate as autonomous multi-step pipelines that use tools and integrate observations into memory.

title: Challenge-Aware Knowledge Recruitment with Meta-Agent Supervision for Medical Multi-Agent Reasoning
summary: This paper proposes a meta-agent supervision approach for medical multi-agent reasoning to improve performance on hard tasks by enabling challenge-aware knowledge recruitment.

title: A Feasibility Condition for Confidence-Gated Tiered LLM Inference
summary: This work explores a feasibility condition for confidence-gated tiered LLM inference, which distributes computation across on-device, edge, and datacenter hardware to achieve cheaper, lower-latency serving.

title: Can Large Language Models Review the Scientific Literature? A Test Against a 102-Article Benchmark
summary: This study assesses the capability of large language models to review scientific literature by testing six AI tools across four stages: finding, interpreting, and synthesizing articles against a 102-article benchmark.

title: SlackBench: Benchmarking Agents on Collaborative Projects Grounded in Real Code Repositories
summary: SlackBench is introduced as a new benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents on complex, collaborative software development projects grounded in real code repositories, addressing limitations of existing benchmarks.

title: MA-SafeDiffuser: Safe Multi-Agent Planning with Diffusion Probabilistic Models
summary: MA-SafeDiffuser proposes a multi-agent extension to SafeDiffuser, enabling safe multi-agent planning by integrating finite-time diffusion invariance guarantees and control barrier functions into diffusion-based trajectory planners.

title: Towards Efficient Whole Page Ranking with One-Pass Inference
summary: This research explores efficient whole-page ranking methods using one-pass inference, aiming to jointly optimize advertisements and organic content while balancing business outcomes and user engagement.

title: Iterated creation, grading, and revision of data science projects by language models
summary: This study evaluates the capability of agentic AI models to complete and iterate on data science projects, with a "writer" model creating and a "grader" model providing feedback.

title: Whose Transparency is it Anyway? Understanding Generative AI Transparency Needs and Gaps Across Stakeholders
summary: This paper investigates the concept of transparency in AI governance, exploring how different stakeholders understand and articulate their needs and gaps regarding generative AI transparency.

title: VirtualTrialHarness: Coordinating Agentic Operationalization of Virtual Trial Protocols Across Complex Clinical Schemas
summary: VirtualTrialHarness is presented as a method for coordinating the agentic operationalization of virtual trial protocols, translating study requirements into executable analyses using clinical data.

title: AGORA: Reliability-Aware Aggregation of LLM Judges via Item-Response Theory
summary: AGORA is a method for reliability-aware aggregation of LLM judges using Item-Response Theory, aiming to improve the accuracy of LLM evaluations compared to costly human assessment.

title: Anduin: A sybil-resistant agentic marketplace reputation system
summary: Anduin is introduced as a sybil-resistant reputation system designed for autonomous AI agents operating in permissionless onchain marketplaces.

title: Verified but Vacuous: Three Failure Surfaces of LLM-Driven Verified Code Generation
summary: This paper analyzes LLM-driven verified code generation, identifying three distinct failure surfaces related to verifier acceptance and syntactic specification binding, arguing against single verification numbers.

title: Hybrid Spark: Adaptive Speculative Decoding That Lets the Content Choose the Drafter
summary: Hybrid Spark proposes an adaptive speculative decoding method for LLM serving that dynamically selects between model-based and model-free drafters based on the workload's content and shape, improving speed.

title: ViBench 2.0: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Software Building
summary: ViBench 2.0 is introduced as a new benchmark for evaluating AI agents on long-horizon software building tasks, reflecting real-world product development on platforms like Replit.

title: Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization for Autonomous AI Agents
summary: This paper introduces Assurance-Conditioned Continuous Authorization (ACCA), an approach for maintaining operational control and authorization for autonomous AI agents as they use tools and delegate tasks.

title: Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents
summary: This research proposes an adaptive memory selection method for LLM agents to address the bottleneck of growing memory costs and improve efficiency in retrieving relevant information.

title: Quantifying Trait-State Hierarchy in EEG Foundation Model and Signal Processing Embeddings
summary: This study quantifies the trait-state hierarchy in EEG data using foundation model and signal processing embeddings to distinguish stable subject characteristics from transient brain states.

title: Grounded but Not Immune: Confirmation Bias in Agent-as-a-judge
summary: This research evaluates confirmation bias in an 'Agent-as-a-judge' system, examining how AI agents tasked with verifying results can be influenced by their own evidence.

title: How Do Artificial Agents Make Decisions in Light of Visual Data?
summary: This study investigates how artificial agents, particularly those powered by Vision-Language Models, make decisions when processing and reasoning with visual data.

title: Agents, Think Only When it Helps
summary: This research explores optimizing LLM agent efficiency by examining the criticality of thought supervision during agent distillation to improve action performance.

title: Self-Supervised Pretraining for Label-Efficient Facial Expression Recognition using Smart Glasses
summary: This item describes using smart glasses, specifically OCOsense, for privacy-preserving Facial Expression Recognition (FER) via self-supervised pretraining.

title: PAYWORTHY: Can LLMs Predict Which Freelance Jobs an AI Agent Will Complete?
summary: This paper introduces PAYWORTHY, a system testing whether large language models can predict an AI agent's success in completing freelance jobs before execution.

title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application
summary: This research presents FlyHash, a new application for LLM agent memory, which uses external memory stores and locality-sensitive hashing for information retention across conversations.

title: Consistency Is Not Understanding: Orbit Audits for Neural Field Weight Readers
summary: This study audits how neural-network weights represent visual content, investigating the separation of functional information from parameter coordinates through neuron permutations.

title: Vision Paper: Why Distributed LLM Post-Training and Decentralized Alignment Are Now Essential
summary: This vision paper argues for distributed and decentralized learning as essential paradigms for LLM post-training and alignment, moving away from centralized preference data assumptions.

title: Auditable Unlearning for LLMs
summary: This research explores auditable machine unlearning for LLMs, focusing on methods to remove user data while retaining model capabilities and robustness against attacks.

title: RECAP: Context-Aware Prediction Recycling with Request-Local and Persistent Memories for Multimodal Speculative Decoding
summary: This paper introduces RECAP, a method for context-aware prediction recycling with request-local and persistent memories to optimize multimodal speculative decoding in vision-language models.

title: EchoKV: Self-Corrective KV Cache Eviction via Iterative Query Feedback
summary: This research introduces EchoKV, a self-corrective KV cache eviction mechanism that uses iterative query feedback to improve memory management in large language models.

title: CHARM+: Cross-Hardware Attention with Re-Merge Multistream Mechanism
summary: This item describes CHARM+, a Cross-Hardware Attention with Re-Merge Multistream Mechanism designed to improve GPU utilization and reduce communication dependencies in distributed LLM training.

title: Routes of Reasoning: Reading and Reshaping Test-Time Compute in MoE Models
summary: This research investigates how to read and reshape test-time compute allocation in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models to prevent inefficient 'overthinking' during reasoning tasks.

title: Split-KV: Efficient Context Parallelism for Training Diffusion Drafters
summary: This paper presents Split-KV, an efficient context parallelism technique for training Diffusion Drafters to accelerate speculative decoding by denoising multiple draft tokens in parallel.

title: Graph-Mediated Large Language Model Systems in the Agentic Era: Reasoning, Knowledge, Retrieval, Execution, and Coordination
summary: This paper discusses the increasing role of graph-mediated systems in LLMs for reasoning, knowledge, retrieval, execution, and multi-agent coordination in the agentic era.

title: From Waste to Discovery: Recycling High-Scored Unexposed Candidates in Taobao Feed Recommendation
summary: This research introduces URED (Unexposed Recycling for Efficient Discovery), a training-free method to recycle high-scored unexposed candidates for improving Taobao's feed recommendation system.

title: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
summary: This item introduces Reglos, a self-evolving personal memory agent that improves its responses and rewrites its memory-to-context harness through recursive self-improvement.

title: Which One Is Sounding? Binaural Sounding Instance Disambiguation for Audio-Visual Segmentation
summary: This research focuses on Binaural Sounding Instance Disambiguation for Audio-Visual Segmentation, aiming to identify specific sounding objects when multiple similar candidates are present.

title: UniCompress: From Multi-LoRA Experts to One Compact Model for Edge Intelligence
summary: This paper presents UniCompress, a deployment-oriented method to create one compact model from multiple LoRA experts for efficient edge intelligence in embodied and edge systems.

title: Reasoning-Trace Overflow in Code Generation: An Empirical Study of Explicit Reasoning Models
summary: This empirical study investigates 'Reasoning-Trace Overflow' in explicit reasoning models for code generation, where models spend excessive output budget on reasoning rather than producing usable code.

title: Beyond Risk Cues: A Mechanism-Level Benchmark and Verifiable Debate for Scam Video Detection on the Web
summary: This paper introduces a mechanism-level benchmark and verifiable debate framework for detecting scam videos online. It aims to provide insights into how scams work and the reasoning behind detection decisions.

title: From Handcrafted to Generative: RLVR-Optimized Icon Generation for Alexa+
summary: This work presents an RLVR-optimized generative system for creating animated icons for Alexa+ devices. It replaces a manual design process, enabling scalable generation of visual reinforcements for conversations.

title: ModalSearcher: Weaving Visual Evidence into Autonomous Cross-Modal Deep Search
summary: ModalSearcher introduces an autonomous cross-modal deep search method that integrates visual evidence into multimodal large language models. It addresses limitations of existing agentic search methods in acquiring novel and knowledge-intensive information.

title: SafeStart: Mitigating the Overlooked Safety Cost of Active Expert Reduction in MoE LLM Serving
summary: SafeStart investigates the safety costs of active expert reduction techniques used in serving Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs. It highlights how these methods can weaken a model's refusal of harmful requests, proposing mitigation strategies.

title: CARM: Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking for Reliable Scientific Super-Resolution
summary: CARM (Conformal Adaptive Risk Masking) is introduced as a method for reliable scientific super-resolution using deep learning. It provides a calibrated rule for identifying reliable spatial regions in reconstructed Earth-observation fields, enhancing accuracy with uncertainty quantification.

title: A Definition of Catastrophic Performance
summary: This paper proposes a definition of catastrophic performance in AI, distinguishing it from merely suboptimal outcomes. It aims to enable rigorous analysis of the impact of objective misspecification on AI system performance.

title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
summary: HarnessFlow presents an MCTS-guided optimization method for designing harnesses that govern LLM agents' interactions with tools and environments. It aims to automate the complex and costly process of harness design to improve agent performance.

title: A Systematic Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Personalized Reasoning of Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper introduces MPRBench, a systematic benchmark designed to evaluate the multimodal personalized reasoning capabilities of vision-language models (MLLMs). It focuses on how these models reason over heterogeneous forms of personal information.

title: DyPSI: Dynamic Physics Sensing via Joint Field and Sensor-Trajectory Generation
summary: DyPSI introduces a method for dynamic physics sensing through joint field and sensor-trajectory generation. It enables the reconstruction of dense spatiotemporal fields from sparse observations in evolving environments and adapts future observation collection.

title: Multi-Resident Data Association in Smart Homes via MDP Modeling and Behavior Cloning
summary: This paper addresses the Multi-Resident Data Association problem in smart homes using MDP modeling and behavior cloning. It aims to identify which resident triggers anonymous sensor events for activity recognition while preserving privacy.

title: Constraint-Preserving Flow Matching for Spectral Graph Generation
summary: This research introduces Constraint-Preserving Flow Matching for spectral graph generation, focusing on modeling graphs through the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of their Laplacians. The method ensures that generated eigensystems retain the structural properties of graph Laplacians.

title: Learning Implicit Solves for Dynamic Simulations
summary: This work introduces the Implicit Neural Operator Solver (INOS) to learn implicit solves for dynamic simulations. INOS pretrains a neural operator and encodes a time integrator, aiming to make high-fidelity simulations more computationally efficient.

title: Matched but Not Better: An Equivalence-Tested Benchmark of Quantum Machine Learning on Six Clinical Datasets and the QML-Health-READY Reporting Framework
summary: This study presents an equivalence-tested benchmark comparing quantum machine learning models with classical models on six clinical datasets. It also introduces the QML-Health-READY Reporting Framework for evaluating quantum machine learning in healthcare.

title: Objective-Conditioned Active Preference Learning for Multi-Objective Alignment
summary: This paper introduces Objective-Conditioned Active Preference Learning to align large language models (LLMs) with multiple objectives like helpfulness and harmlessness. The method aims to reduce annotation costs by intelligently selecting preference judgments.

title: TSFM Meets LLM: Context as Covariates
summary: This work explores integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) with Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) by using textual context as covariates. The goal is to leverage predictive signals from textual information in time series datasets.

title: The Confidence Score: a New Measure on Kernels
summary: This paper introduces "The Confidence Score," a new measure for evaluating kernels in machine learning. It is designed to tune hyperparameters, select candidate kernels, and assess kernel suitability for classification tasks.

title: Recasting Visual Language Models as EEG Foundation Models for Clinical Neurodiagnostics
summary: This research proposes recasting visual language models as EEG foundation models for clinical neurodiagnostics. It aims to create a unified representation for multiple EEG-specific tasks, moving beyond traditional task-specific supervised models.

title: Support Vector Machines Directly Minimise KL Divergence
summary: This paper presents a new theoretical finding that Support Vector Machines (SVMs) directly minimize KL Divergence. This provides a probabilistic interpretation for SVMs, bridging them with probabilistic machine learning models.

title: Exploring the Privacy--Size Tradeoff for Differentially Private Self-Attentive Variational Autoencoders
summary: This research explores the privacy-size tradeoff for Differentially Private Self-Attentive Variational Autoencoders used for generating synthetic data. It investigates how the privacy budget affects data utility while adhering to privacy obligations.

title: C-GRPO: Conformal Group Relative Policy Optimization
summary: C-GRPO (Conformal Group Relative Policy Optimization) is introduced as a new optimization method for training reasoning-oriented language models. It addresses the inefficiencies of fixed group sizes in standard GRPO by adapting budget allocation for on-policy rollouts.

title: Relevance Propagation as Entropic Optimal Transport on Filippov Neural Networks: Sinkhorn Propagation and Region Relevance in Image Classifiers
summary: This paper redefines relevance propagation in neural networks as an optimal transport problem, offering a variational framework for understanding Layer-wise Relevance Propagation (LRP).

title: Transport along Local Annealing Paths: Wasserstein Geometry and Multimodal Sampling
summary: This research proposes learning transport along prescribed annealing paths to mitigate mode collapse in variational approaches for multimodal sampling, analyzing the geometric properties of such paths.

title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
summary: This paper investigates the generalization limitations of multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) for post-reinforcement learning consolidation, revealing that high in-distribution performance can mask incomplete capability consolidation.

title: LACS: Distribution-Sensitive Label-Agnostic Confidence Selection for Dynamic Data Pruning
summary: This work introduces LACS (Label-Agnostic Confidence Selection), a distribution-sensitive method for dynamic data pruning that adapts confidence thresholds to efficiently select training examples.

title: Data-Efficient Scaling-Law Discovery for Recommendation Systems via Coupled Hyperparameter Scaling
summary: This research presents a data-efficient approach to discovering scaling laws for recommendation systems by analyzing coupled hyperparameter scaling, improving upon traditional methods for heterogeneous architectures.

title: When Are Two SAE Latents the Same Feature?
summary: This paper develops a framework using energy-weighted optimal transport to compare sparse autoencoders (SAEs), addressing feature correspondence, dictionary differences, and evaluation uncertainty.

title: Adaptive Domain Decomposition for Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks
summary: This work introduces Adaptive Domain Decomposition Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks (ADD-FBPINNs), integrating data-driven domain partitioning with physics-informed networks for enhanced performance.

title: Revisiting Critic Estimation in Soft Actor-Critic Algorithms
summary: This paper revisits critic estimation in Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithms, exploring alternative Q-function learning designs beyond standard one-step temporal-difference methods.

title: CoReFlow: Consistency-Relaxed Flow Maps for Probabilistic Traffic Forecasting
summary: This paper proposes CoReFlow, a method using consistency-relaxed flow maps to improve probabilistic traffic forecasting by better capturing uncertainties in complex road networks.

title: Give the Drafter a Second Chance to Guess: Parallel Reconsideration for Speculative Decoding
summary: This research introduces 'parallel reconsideration' for speculative decoding, allowing a small drafter model to make multiple guesses per token to accelerate large language model inference.

title: Do Language Models Know Which Constraints Belong Together?
summary: This paper explores whether language models can identify which constraint families should be combined for effective Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation in mixed-integer programs, a crucial step for strengthening linear relaxations.

title: RESHPart: Feedback-Reshaped Spectral Embedding for Hypergraph Partitioning
summary: This work presents RESHPart, a new approach to spectral hypergraph partitioning that uses feedback-reshaped spectral embedding to achieve higher quality partitions by refining geometric representations.

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Universal Latent Spaces for Operator Learning
summary: This paper proposes self-supervised learning for neural operators to create universal latent spaces, enabling shareable representations across different tasks without rebuilding reduced spaces from labeled data.

title: Text-Only Domain Adaptation for Low-Resource Medical ASR: Shallow Fusion and Density Ratio Rescoring for Hausa
summary: This research investigates text-only domain adaptation techniques, such as shallow fusion and density ratio rescoring, to improve automatic speech recognition (ASR) for low-resource medical contexts in Hausa.

title: Pathwise-Budgeted LLM Routing: Online Allocation with K-Bit Tail-Cost Learning
summary: This paper addresses pathwise-budgeted LLM routing, proposing an online allocation strategy with K-Bit tail-cost learning to maximize the number of served tasks under a fixed budget.

title: PEARL: Prediction Error-Adaptive Regularized Learning for Selective Forgetting under Partial Preference Drift
summary: This paper introduces PEARL (Prediction Error-Adaptive Regularized Learning), a method for selective forgetting that adapts to partial preference drift in personalized systems without uniform forgetting.

title: Deep Meets Classical: A CPU-Efficient Decision-Fusion Model for Automatic Modulation Classification
summary: This work presents a CPU-efficient decision-fusion model that combines deep learning and classical methods for automatic modulation classification in cognitive radio applications.

title: Reward Budgeting Reduces Premature Convergence in Reinforcement Learning for LLM Reasoning
summary: This research introduces reward budgeting as a technique to reduce premature convergence and improve performance in reinforcement learning for large language model reasoning tasks.

title: On the Design of Hyper-Connections: Simplification, Stability, and Scalability
summary: This paper systematically studies Hyper-Connections (HC) architectures in language models to understand their components, aiming for simplification, improved stability, and better scalability.

title: A Comparative Study of Importance Attribution to Columns in Deep Learning over Relational Databases
summary: This paper conducts a comparative study of explanation methods that assign importance scores to database attributes in deep learning models trained on relational databases.

title: Decouple to Reuse: Fine-Grained Knowledge Augmentation for Time Series Foundation Models
summary: This paper proposes fine-grained knowledge augmentation to improve time series foundation models, specifically addressing challenges in applying pre-trained models to downstream tasks using retrieval-augmented approaches.

title: Attraction-Ranking Mismatch in Out-of-Distribution Detection: Theory and Evidence from Hamiltonian Feature Dynamics
summary: This research investigates the effectiveness of attracting features toward in-distribution regions for out-of-distribution detection, using Hamiltonian dynamics as a controlled testbed to analyze attraction-ranking mismatch.

title: Who Pays for the Knowledge Models Copy? Model Collapse as Rogers' Paradox
summary: This paper examines the phenomenon of 'model collapse' in generative models, where knowledge is lost across generations when models are trained on their own outputs, and discusses theoretical implications and remedies.

title: Act-HiMotif: Hierarchical Daily Activity Schedule Generation via Learned Activity-Structure Motifs
summary: This research introduces Act-HiMotif, a method for generating hierarchical daily activity schedules from individual attributes using learned activity-structure motifs, aiming to improve human behavior simulation and travel modeling.

title: Learning From Static Context in Federated Time Series Forecasting
summary: This paper explores learning from static context in federated time series forecasting, where global models are trained across heterogeneous series without centralizing raw data, leveraging federated learning.

title: PRISM-AMC: Replay-Free Continual Learning for Automatic Modulation Classification
summary: This research proposes PRISM-AMC, a replay-free continual learning approach for Automatic Modulation Classification (AMC), addressing challenges in adapting to new modulation classes without access to past training data.

title: Shallow Encoding Emits Deep Memories
summary: This paper investigates how hybrid language models manage memory, specifically through key-value caches and fixed-size recurrent states in their layers to retain knowledge of earlier tokens.

title: Learning When to Think Aloud in Latent Reasoning
summary: This research explores a method for 'Learning When to Think Aloud' in latent reasoning, aiming to improve the precision of Chain-of-Thought approaches for tasks like mathematical reasoning by selectively externalizing intermediate steps.

title: Short-Term Forecasting of Heterogeneous Wind Power Fleets: Global Temporal Fusion Transformer Leveraging Static Covariates
summary: This study investigates short-term forecasting for heterogeneous wind power fleets using a global Temporal Fusion Transformer that leverages static covariates, aiming to improve grid stability and electricity trading.

title: Neural Stochastic Forecasting for Lateral Molecular Diffusion Simulations
summary: This research introduces a neural stochastic (NS) model for forecasting lateral molecular diffusion, offering a computationally efficient method for predicting long-time diffusion of membrane proteins compared to traditional simulations.

title: Selective Prediction Intervals: Jointly Learning to Predict, Bound, and Abstain
summary: This paper proposes 'Selective Prediction Intervals,' a deep learning method that jointly learns to provide point estimates, bound risks with intervals, and offer an option to abstain for high-stakes regression decisions.

title: FaCoDiff: Factor-Correlated Diffusion for Multivariate Probabilistic Forecasting
summary: This research introduces Factor-Correlated Diffusion (FaCoDiff), a novel approach for multivariate probabilistic forecasting that models cross-variable dependence while managing marginal noise scales and covariance costs.

title: Cross-Asset Knowledge Transfer for Early Fault Detection of Data-Scarce Assets Without Target Fault Data
summary: This paper addresses early fault detection in data-scarce industrial assets by investigating cross-asset knowledge transfer methods, aiming to improve reliability management even without target fault data.

title: Rubric Curriculum RL: Exploiting the Generation-Verification Gap in Non-Verifiable Domains
summary: This research proposes 'Rubric Curriculum RL,' a method to exploit the generation-verification gap in non-verifiable domains, extending the gains of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to open-ended tasks.

title: Ukradne tvář i hlas během sekund. Češi našli způsob, jak se bránit umělé inteligenci
summary: A Czech entrepreneur and a Stanford researcher developed Synhawk, a startup creating technology to detect sophisticated AI-powered fraud and fake content, aiming for global market presence.

title: DS@GT ARC at CheckThat! 2026: A Verdict-Anchored Pipeline for Generating Fact-Checking Articles
summary: This paper details a 'Verdict-Anchored Pipeline' for generating fact-checking articles, developed by the DS@GT ARC team for CLEF 2026 CheckThat! Lab Task 3, to automate the production of fact-checking content.

title: CCDWIKI: Decoupling Case Formulation from Response Generation in Longitudinal CBT Dialogue
summary: This research introduces CCDWIKI, a method for decoupling case formulation from response generation in longitudinal Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) dialogue systems.

title: Human-like cross-language generalisation in deep neural speaker embeddings and its acoustic foundations
summary: This study investigates human-like cross-language generalization in deep neural speaker embeddings and its underlying acoustic foundations, exploring how these embeddings perform across different languages.

title: Same Origin, Different Verdicts: Text Production Conditions Confound Machine-Generated Text Detection in Russian
summary: This research examines how text production conditions can confound the automated detection of machine-generated text, specifically in Russian, highlighting that origin is a property of the process, not just the text itself.

title: SRRM: A Retrieval-Reconstruction Benchmark for Evaluating Long-Context Memory in Small Language Models
summary: This paper introduces SRRM, a new Retrieval-Reconstruction Benchmark designed to evaluate the long-context memory capabilities of Small Language Models (SLMs) in preserving information.

title: AI-Driven SaaS Platform Integration: AI Express for Unified Generative AI Services with Pay-As-You-Go Credit Systems and Scalable Microservice Architecture
summary: AI Express is a SaaS platform designed to consolidate various generative AI services into a single, pay-as-you-go offering, aiming to reduce costs and streamline workflows for users.

title: When to Ask, When to Answer: Strategic Clarification for Ambiguous Reference Resolution in Dialogue
summary: This research examines how large language models (LLMs) tend to answer prematurely in dialogue and proposes strategic clarification methods for ambiguous reference resolution.

title: Rewrite, Then Veto: Rewriter-Agnostic Edit Gating for LLM-Based Post-OCR Correction
summary: This paper proposes EditVeto, a method using a veto gate after an LLM rewrite to correct noisy OCR transcripts without altering already correct text.

title: RAGCompass: Generalizable Retriever Routing via Reranking
summary: RAGCompass is a method designed to improve retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) by dynamically selecting the most suitable retriever for a given query through reranking.

title: Contextual Pictograms for Repairing Multilingual ASR Errors
summary: This work describes an interface that uses alternative transcripts, replay, and contextual pictograms to help users recognize and repair errors in multilingual ASR outputs.

title: Cognitive Bias Signatures in Search-Equipped LLM Agents: A Stage-Resolved Analysis
summary: This study develops a controlled search harness to examine cognitive bias in search-equipped LLM agents, exploring how initial conditions influence their search and evidence use.

title: Prospective Memory for Proactive LLM Agents
summary: This paper introduces the concept of prospective memory for proactive LLM agents, enabling them to retain future-directed intentions and act on them when appropriate opportunities arise.

title: How Well Can Large Language Models Impersonate Individual Authors? A Comparative Evaluation
summary: This study provides a comparative evaluation of six large language models (LLMs) on their ability to impersonate individual authors using product review texts.

title: Phonological Knowledge of Chinese Characters in Language Models
summary: This research introduces PinyinBench, a new benchmark to evaluate the phonological knowledge of language models concerning Chinese characters, including homophones and polyphonic characters.

title: Matching the Training-Time Weight Rule in Inference-Time Expert Deactivation
summary: This paper compares different implementations of expert deactivation at inference time, such as removal and freezing, and their effects on token routing and expert weights in models.

title: Learning When Human Decisions Matter: Executor-Relative Consultation Value for LLM Agents
summary: This research formulates a method for allocating human decision capacity in tasks involving LLM agents, focusing on when human input provides essential context or judgment.

title: TandemBench: Benchmarking Decision Models for Multi-Agent Collaboration
summary: TandemBench is introduced as a new benchmark with 1,200 questions designed to evaluate decision models in multi-agent collaboration scenarios, such as cooking.

title: CARTBench: Rubric-Based Evaluation of Shopping Advice for Complex and Ambiguous Requests with Timelines
summary: CARTBench is presented as a new rubric-based benchmark for evaluating LLM shopping assistants on their ability to provide advice for complex and ambiguous requests with timelines.

title: When Does Better Confidence Improve a Knowledge-Graph Audit?
summary: This study investigates how confidence estimates guide human review in LLM-built knowledge graphs, analyzing factors like repairability and selection headroom that affect audit improvement.

title: Information-Matched Auditing of Conversational Emotion-Shift Forecasting: A Leakage-Safe Evaluation Protocol
summary: This paper proposes an information-matched auditing method and a leakage-safe evaluation protocol for comparing models in conversational emotion-shift forecasting, preventing distorted results.

title: Selective, Risk-Controlled Emotion Forecasting in Conversation: From a Persistence Barrier to Departure Detection with Conformal Guarantees
summary: This research proposes a learnable and deployable reformulation for forecasting emotion in conversation, moving from predicting the next emotional state to detecting emotional departure with guarantees.

title: Familiar letters, not related languages, let unseen languages into a shared space of meaning
summary: This study finds that familiar letter systems, rather than related languages, are key for AI models to incorporate unseen languages into a shared semantic space.

title: When Every Choice Is Correct: A Causal Study of Numerical Preference in Language Models
summary: This causal study investigates numerical preference in language models when all choices are valid, analyzing how preferences are processed across layers and tokens.

title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
summary: Confucius4-R2T2 is introduced as a new stable-prefix streaming ASR model designed for real real-time transcription, aiming to reduce wasted work from token revisions.

title: Adapting Qwen3 to Tajik from 0.6B to 8B: Lower Text Loss Did Not Mean Better Understanding
summary: This research investigates adapting the Qwen3 model to Tajik using LoRA adapters, finding that while text loss decreased, reading comprehension did not improve significantly.

title: ProcessPrefBench: Evaluating Cross-Task Transfer of Individual Process Preferences from Naturalistic Human-AI Interaction
summary: This paper introduces ProcessPrefBench, a benchmark designed to evaluate how AI systems learn and transfer individual user process preferences from natural human-AI dialogue interactions across different tasks.

title: Overview of the NTCIR-19 SciClaimEval Task: Cross-modal Claim Verification in Scientific Papers
summary: This paper provides an overview of SciClaimEval, a new pilot task at NTCIR-19 for verifying scientific claims against information presented in tables and figures within academic papers.

title: The Harness Is the Model: Agent Scaffolding Changes a Fixed LLM's Compliance with Banking Conduct Rules, Unevenly Across Models
summary: This research investigates how an agent's 'harness' or scaffolding, including tool calls and checks, influences a fixed large language model's compliance with banking conduct rules, demonstrating varied impacts across models.

title: Accelerating Long-Context Decoding in Large-Scale Hybrid LLMs Without Retraining
summary: This work explores methods to accelerate long-context decoding in large-scale hybrid language models by using linear-attention layers, without requiring retraining the model, to improve efficiency.

title: AssameseLM-E2B: An Open-Weight Assamese Language Model for Efficient Consumer-Grade Deployment
summary: This paper introduces AssameseLM-E2B, an open-weight large language model and its instruction-tuned variant, designed to improve performance in low-resource languages like Assamese for efficient consumer-grade deployment.

title: Editing Large Language Models with Geometry-Aware Regularization
summary: This research proposes a new knowledge editing method for large language models that uses geometry-aware regularization to improve the updating of knowledge while preserving the structural integrity of the knowledge representation.

title: Loop Before You Leap: What Recurrent Depth Can and Cannot Buy in Data-Limited Pretraining
summary: This research investigates the effectiveness of additional recurrent computation in multimodal models during data-limited pretraining to close the performance gap with text-only baselines by reusing layers without increasing parameters.

title: Mass Producing Training Data with Surprising Side Effects
summary: This study examines how the mass production of training data can lead to surprising and unintended side effects on language model behavior, including misalignment and persona induction, making generalization challenging to understand.

title: Training-Free Character-Length Control in Summarization with Diffusion Language Models
summary: This paper introduces a training-free method for precise character-length control in summarization tasks using diffusion language models, addressing a common challenge for autoregressive LMs in generating fixed-length outputs.

title: Presentation Sensitivity in Typed Decision Models for Subjective Text Evaluation
summary: This paper presents an audit of presentation sensitivity in typed decision models (Jev, Clef Flash, Perplexity Decider) used for subjective text evaluation, examining how interface design influences results.

title: Interpretable Text Embeddings Based on Hierarchical Questions
summary: This paper describes a method for generating interpretable text embeddings using hierarchical question-answering, which represents texts as vectors of yes/no answers for detailed information and high task performance.

title: Ruby-OPD: Enhancing Pronunciation Controllability and Accuracy for Flow-Matching Text-to-Speech via On-Policy Distillation
summary: This paper presents Ruby-OPD, a method using on-policy distillation to enhance pronunciation accuracy and fine-grained controllability in flow-matching Text-to-Speech systems for Japanese, a complex unsegmented language.

title: Twists and Turns: A Graph-Based Benchmark and Framework for Long-Term Memory in Exploration Tasks
summary: This paper introduces a graph-based benchmark and framework called 'Twists and Turns' for evaluating long-term memory capabilities of models in exploration tasks such as scientific research and software development.

title: ArcRAG: Agentic Compositional Retrieval over Knowledge Graphs
summary: This paper introduces ArcRAG, an agentic compositional retrieval system that uses knowledge graphs to answer questions, focusing on how retrieval strategies perform under changes in graph construction.

title: LibriSpeech-Real-QA: A Benchmark for Streaming Question Answering
summary: This paper introduces LibriSpeech-Real-QA, a new benchmark designed to evaluate speech large language models in streaming question-answering scenarios, addressing the need for real-time interaction in many applications.

title: CRESiST: Self-Enhancing Explorative Policy Learning for Simultaneous Speech Translation
summary: This paper introduces CRESiST, a system for self-enhancing explorative policy learning in simultaneous speech translation, aiming to balance translation quality and latency in LLM-based systems.

title: Dialect Matters: A Dialect-Aware Baseline for Igala-English Machine Translation
summary: This paper establishes a dialect-aware baseline for Igala-English machine translation, addressing the challenges of developing intelligent systems for low-resource languages with dialectal variations.

title: When Do Summaries Become Instructions? Unsupported Policy in LLM Agents' Self-Written Handoff Summaries
summary: This research investigates how LLM agents' self-written handoff summaries can contain unsupported policies that influence the behavior of subsequent agent instances, and where these policies originate.

title: Replicability, Reproducibility, and Robustness in Political and Social Science Research with Large Language Models
summary: This chapter addresses the challenges of replicability, reproducibility, and robustness in political and social science research that uses large language models, highlighting issues stemming from probabilistic and variable LLM outputs.

title: ALTO: African and Levantine Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence Corpus
summary: This paper introduces ALTO, a new corpus for detecting Tech-Facilitated Gender-Based Violence (TFGBV) in African and Levantine languages, aiming to address the data imbalance in current models for harm detection.

title: Reasoning over Non-Parametric Memory in Multilingual LLMs: A Cognitive-Based Analysis of Relational Knowledge
summary: This paper studies how multilingual LLMs reason over relational knowledge provided in their context via Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), analyzing evidence-conditioned reasoning.

title: Ranking Agreement Does Not Reveal Paragraph-Edit Agreement in Two Released Paper Acceptance Predictors
summary: This research evaluates if agreement on existing papers supports using fast acceptance classifiers for selecting revisions, comparing a word/document feature classifier with two text-only acceptance predictors.

title: Measuring Risk, Not Harm: Detecting Psychological Harm Risk Factors in LLM Conversations
summary: This paper proposes a method to detect psychological harm risk factors in LLM conversations by identifying observable AI behaviors, as direct monitoring of harm is difficult.

title: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting
summary: This research benchmarks the temporal self-knowledge of LLMs for financial backtesting, assessing whether models know the outcomes they are asked to predict given their knowledge cutoff.

title: SAUCE: Summary Analysis Using Conversation Entailment
summary: This paper introduces SAUCE, a reference-free, fact-based evaluation pipeline for assessing the performance of Large Language Models in summarizing and evaluating cross-lingual conversational speech.

title: LooM: Loop-Invariant Memory for Causal Encoder-Decoder Language Models
summary: This paper proposes LooM (Loop-invariant Memory) to address memory growth and other limitations in Looped Transformers, aiming to improve causal encoder-decoder language models.

title: Before You Continue: Evaluating Time-Sensitive Safety Awareness in Conversational Assistants
summary: This research focuses on evaluating the time-sensitive safety awareness of conversational LLM assistants, assessing their ability to recognize and adjust advice based on implicit time-dependent constraints.

title: Persona Perspectives: Adopting Viewpoints Reorganizes Representations in LLMs
summary: This paper investigates how adopting different "personas" reorganizes internal representations in Large Language Models (LLMs), challenging assumptions of consistent feature representation across contexts.

title: Balancing hierarchical representation and quantization: A performance trade-off in text embeddings
summary: This empirical benchmark study evaluates the interaction and performance trade-offs between hierarchical text embedding models and quantization techniques across 38 tasks, focusing on computational efficiency.

title: VAR-Q: Tuning-free KV Cache Quantization for Visual Autoregressive Image and Video Generation
summary: This paper introduces VAR-Q, a tuning-free KV cache quantization method for visual autoregressive image and video generation, designed to manage KV memory for block-by-block decoding.

title: Visual Forensic Detection of Fabricated Bangla News Photocards using Deep Learning
summary: This research applies deep learning for visual forensic detection of fabricated Bangla news photocards, addressing localized misinformation spread through single-image news summaries.

title: mmHand: Toward Pixel-Level-Accuracy Hand Localization Using a Single Commodity mmWave Device
summary: This paper presents mmHand, a method for achieving pixel-level-accuracy hand localization using a single commodity mmWave device, addressing limitations in existing hand localization technologies.

title: When Does Sharing Work? Scaling a Shared SigLIP2 Across Image, Video, Audio, and Audio-Visual Representations
summary: This paper introduces Omni-Encoder, a general multimodal encoder model that scales a shared SigLIP2 across image, video, audio, and audio-visual representations for improved cross-modal understanding.

title: PEEK: One-Step-Look-Ahead Exposure Bias Correction for Diffusion Sampling
summary: This paper introduces PEEK, a one-step-look-ahead exposure bias correction method designed to improve the sampling process in diffusion image generators by addressing the train-test gap.

title: Augmentation with Reinforcement Transformation for Low-textured Scientific Sketch Image Retrieval
summary: This research proposes an augmentation method using reinforcement transformation to improve image retrieval for challenging low-textured scientific sketch images in various applications.

title: PointNDF: Cascaded Neural Displacement Fields for Point Cloud Denoising
summary: This paper introduces PointNDF, a method utilizing cascaded neural displacement fields for point cloud denoising, aiming to recover clean 3D geometry while preserving fine surface details.

title: SO(3)-Equivariant Learning on CAD Boundary Representations
summary: This research explores SO(3)-Equivariant Learning for CAD Boundary Representations (B-reps) to improve robustness to part pose, addressing limitations of existing B-rep networks under rotation.

title: From Tokens to Trajectories: Parameter-Efficient Continuous Adaptation of Unified Multimodal Models
summary: This paper introduces FlowShift, a parameter-efficient method for continuous adaptation of Unified Multimodal Models (UMMs), aiming to overcome the quantization bottleneck that degrades fine visual details.

title: From Activation to Intervention: Interpreting Sparse Visual Features through Reconstruction
summary: This research explores interpreting sparse visual features in Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) through reconstruction, aiming to better understand and explain model behavior.

title: How Finely Can Vision-Language Models See Biology? Bio-VQA: A Benchmark for Taxonomic, Morphological, Spatial and Individual Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces Bio-VQA, a new benchmark designed to evaluate how finely Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can perform taxonomic, morphological, spatial, and individual reasoning in biology for biodiversity monitoring.

title: Lesion Overlap Ranks PET Segmentation Models but Does Not Certify Patient-Level Tumor Burden
summary: This item evaluates PET segmentation models using overlap metrics to rank their performance, highlighting the need for patient-level reliability metrics beyond standard benchmarks.

title: Discarded or Unreachable? Diagnosing and Repairing Spatial Relation Failure in Vision--Language Similarity
summary: This research diagnoses spatial relation failures in vision-language models, identifying whether the issue lies in the accessibility of relations or their discard during pooling, and suggests different repair strategies.

title: Role-based Effectiveness of an Epistemic Uncertainty Estimate in Training Models for Semantic Segmentation of 3D LiDAR Point Clouds
summary: This paper investigates the effectiveness of epistemic uncertainty estimates in training models for semantic segmentation of 3D LiDAR point clouds, addressing challenges due to sparsity and noise in data.

title: Whose Values Are Generated? Measuring Visual Value Leakage in Multilingual Text-to-Image Generation
summary: This research focuses on measuring 'visual value leakage' in multilingual text-to-image generation systems, evaluating how cultural values are implicitly conveyed in generated images beyond recognizable elements.

title: Multimodal Fusion Methods for Whole-Slide Images and Clinical Data in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
summary: This paper presents a modular framework for comparing multimodal AI fusion methods for whole-slide images and clinical data in computational pathology, specifically for Inflammatory Bowel Disease.

title: GaussianRenderFormer: Transformer-based Rendering of 3D Gaussian Splats
summary: GaussianRenderFormer is a new transformer-based AI model that can directly render 3D Gaussian splats from a set of Gaussians and a camera view, without needing a traditional rasterizer.

title: CAPTOR: text-encoder-free grounding by counting caption co-occurrence over the visual words of a frozen encoder
summary: CAPTOR is a new method for text-encoder-free grounding of text queries in images by counting caption co-occurrence over the visual words of a frozen encoder, addressing a limitation in vision-language models.

title: Spatio-Temporal Multi-Order Interaction for Video Recognition
summary: This paper proposes a new method for Spatio-Temporal Multi-Order Interaction for video recognition, aiming to reduce computational overhead caused by explicit cross-channel aggregation projections.

title: ARIDA - Active railway infrastructure dataset annotation using neural network predictions
summary: ARIDA is an Active Railway Infrastructure Dataset Annotation framework that uses neural network predictions to assist in creating large image datasets for railway perception, particularly for complex geometries.

title: NitroFusion2: Bringing Adversarial Loss to the Text Stream of Multimodal Diffusion Transformers
summary: NitroFusion2 introduces Text-Stream Adversarial Distillation (TSAD) to multimodal diffusion transformers, applying adversarial loss to the text stream for enhanced image-dependent conditioning.

title: Toward an Optimal Configuration for Tree Species Classification from Bark Images: A Leakage-Safe Ablation Study
summary: This study conducts a leakage-safe ablation study to determine optimal configurations for deep-learning approaches in automatically classifying tree species from bark images.

title: TRUST-Stereo: Teacher-Assisted Robust Uncertainty-Guided Search and Transfer for Fast Stereo Matching
summary: TRUST-Stereo proposes a Teacher-Assisted Robust Uncertainty-Guided Search and Transfer method to improve fast stereo matching by addressing sensitivity to errors in propagated disparity.

title: Anchored Slice Propagation with Boundary Transport for 3D CT Segmentation from Three Orthogonal Annotated Slices
summary: This research presents Anchored Slice Propagation with Boundary Transport, a new method for 3D CT segmentation that uses three orthogonal annotated slices to improve mask propagation reliability.

title: GeoDIVE: Geospatial Descent Informed by Value Estimation
summary: GeoDIVE is a new system designed for geospatial descent informed by value estimation, used to efficiently find specific objects and patterns in large regions for applications like agriculture and disaster response.

title: Mitigating Spurious Invariance in Contrastive Learning: A Probabilistic Self-Supervised Learning Framework for Medical Image Analysis
summary: This paper introduces a probabilistic self-supervised learning framework to mitigate spurious invariance in contrastive learning, aiming to improve medical image analysis without extensive manual annotation.

title: C-WFDM: A ControlNet-Guided Wavelet-Fusion Diffusion Model for Multimodal Brain MRI Completion
summary: C-WFDM is a new ControlNet-Guided Wavelet-Fusion Diffusion Model developed for multimodal brain MRI completion, addressing data availability imbalances in neuroimaging datasets.

title: Learning Hierarchical Patch Splitting Policies for Faster Vision Transformers
summary: This research focuses on learning hierarchical patch splitting policies to make Vision Transformers faster by adaptively adjusting patch sizes based on image content, reducing token sequence length.

title: Decompose the Distillation: Interpretable Single-Pass Guidance for Diffusion Models
summary: This paper introduces Interpretable Single-Pass Guidance for diffusion models, a method that decomposes distillation to provide a more flexible and efficient guidance rule for conditional image generation.

title: ME^2FDiff: Multiscale Expert Enhancing Feature Diffusion in Residual Network for Brain Tumor Segmentation
summary: ME^2FDiff is a Multiscale Expert Enhancing Feature Diffusion in Residual Network model developed for automated brain tumor segmentation from MRI, addressing challenges from post-treatment structural changes.

title: WayPOP: A Panoramic Open-Set Panoptic Tracking Benchmark
summary: WayPOP is introduced as a new Panoramic Open-Set Panoptic Tracking Benchmark designed to evaluate holistic perception in autonomous agents, including tracking objects outside a fixed semantic taxonomy across views.

title: GREP: Grounding Generated Room Evaluation in Principles
summary: This paper introduces GREP, a new evaluation framework to assess the overall quality of AI-generated furnished rooms, addressing limitations in current evaluation methods.

title: ReTailor: A Residual Feature Tailoring Framework for Real-Time Cross-Sensor Pansharpening Adaptation
summary: This paper presents ReTailor, a framework for adapting pansharpening models to new sensors in real-time without extensive retraining or target-sensor specific data.

title: Navigational Safety of Marine Surface Vehicles in Restricted Visibility: From Intelligent Vision to Vision-Centered Multi-Sensor Fusion
summary: This paper explores enhancing the navigational safety of marine surface vehicles in restricted visibility by using intelligent vision and multi-sensor fusion systems.

title: DualCast: Dual-Image Conditioned Diffusion Transformers for Digital Human E-Commerce Video Generation
summary: This paper introduces DualCast, a diffusion transformer model that generates e-commerce videos of digital humans, preserving product appearance, human identity, and video style.

title: Generative AI for urban planning: synthesizing land-use maps with satellite imagery via DualControlNet
summary: This paper explores using generative AI with DualControlNet to synthesize new land-use maps from satellite imagery for urban planning, moving beyond predictive models.

title: Feature Puzzles: Single-Image Supervision for Multi-View 3D-Aware Segmentation
summary: This paper proposes 'Feature Puzzles,' a method for achieving multi-view 3D-aware segmentation using only single-image supervision, reducing the need for expensive video or multi-view data.

title: Chronos: Sequential Identity-Preserving Video Generation by Temporal Anchoring
summary: This paper introduces Chronos, a method for sequential identity-preserving video generation that synthesizes high-quality videos while maintaining subject identity across various motions.

title: DecoupAttn: Decoupled Sparse Attention for Training-Free Acceleration of Video Diffusion
summary: This paper proposes DecoupAttn, a decoupled sparse attention mechanism that provides training-free acceleration for video diffusion transformers by optimizing key block computations.

title: Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal Large Language Models
summary: This paper introduces modality-aware expert pruning for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) based multimodal large language models to significantly reduce their memory footprint.

title: CLEAR: Color-Texture Latent Alignment for Single Image Reflection Removal
summary: This paper presents CLEAR, a method for single image reflection removal that uses color-texture latent alignment to recover transmitted scenes from photographs captured through glass.

title: PathoS2VD: From 2D Histopathology to Pseudo Z-Stack Representations
summary: This paper introduces PathoS2VD, a method that generates pseudo Z-stack representations from 2D histopathology images, addressing the inherent 3D morphology of biological tissues.

title: Clips2Story: Training-Free Video Storyboarding and Editing Using Multimodal Retrieval-Embedded Generation
summary: This paper proposes Clips2Story, a training-free method for video storyboarding and editing that uses multimodal retrieval-embedded generation to organize fragmented footage into coherent narratives.

title: FedIA: Instance-Aware Cross-Modal Representations for Federated Prompt Learning
summary: This paper introduces FedIA, a method that uses instance-aware cross-modal representations for federated prompt learning, enabling efficient adaptation of vision-language models across decentralized clients.

title: Intra-Architecture Source Attribution for Stable Diffusion: A New Task with Benchmark Dataset and Baseline
summary: This paper introduces a new task, benchmark dataset, and baseline for intra-architecture source attribution, aiming to identify the specific source model for images generated by Stable Diffusion.

title: MotoVerse: A Benchmark for Predictive Perception of Motorized Two-Wheelers in Dense Unstructured Traffic
summary: This paper introduces MotoVerse, a new benchmark dataset for predictive perception of motorized two-wheelers in dense traffic, aiming to advance research for autonomous driving and ADAS in this domain.

title: ChanSFormer: A Channel Agnostic Vision Transformer for Multi-Channel Cell Painting Images
summary: This paper presents ChanSFormer, a channel-agnostic vision transformer designed for multi-channel cell painting images and other heterogeneous multi-channel imaging data in scientific pipelines.

title: METRIC-GS: Selective Metric-Scale Estimation for 3D Gaussian Splatting
summary: This paper introduces METRIC-GS, a method for selective metric-scale estimation in 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstructions, allowing for accurate measurements and AR content placement.

title: USI-Brain: Enhancing Underwater Spatial Intelligence via Spatial Data-Driven Vision-Language Modeling
summary: This paper proposes USI-Brain, a framework that enhances underwater spatial intelligence by leveraging spatial data-driven vision-language modeling to overcome visual challenges in underwater environments.

title: UniRestorer++: Scalable Universal Image Restoration with Multi-Granularity Degradation Modeling
summary: This paper introduces UniRestorer++, a method for scalable universal image restoration that handles diverse degradations within a single model through multi-granularity degradation modeling.

title: RI-Prune: Relation and Information Aware Visual Token Pruning for Multi-Image Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper introduces RI-Prune, a relation and information-aware visual token pruning method for multi-image vision-language models to improve efficiency by managing the increased visual token budget.

title: SVGFaith: A Two-Layer Meta-Evaluation of Faithfulness Metrics for Text-to-SVG Generation
summary: Text-to-SVG systems are commonly evaluated by applying raster-image metrics to rasterised outputs, yet whether these scores capture fine-grained prompt faithfulness remains unclear. We introduce SVGFaith, a two-layer meta-evaluation framework in which the more faithful candidate of each pair is determined by construction or by human judgment. SVGFaith-Diagnostic contains 1,842 controlled contrastive pairs across eight capability axes, split evenly between two directions: two renderings compared against one prompt, and two descriptions compared against one rendering. SVGFaith-Arena contains 1,327 human-annotated comparisons of real generator outputs. On SVGFaith-Diagnostic, CLIP and three other image--text embedding metrics reach at least 0.789 pairwise accuracy on object identity but at most 0.672 on spatial relations and attribute binding, where chance is 0.5. We further introduce SVGFaith-Score, an interpretable pointwise metric. A domain-tuned decomposer turns each prompt into a dependency graph of atomic visual requirements, a visual question answering model scores whether each requirement is satisfied, and a requirement's score is discounted when its prerequisites score low. In addition to the overall score, the per-requirement scores show which requirements are judged unsatisfied and which inherit discounts from their prerequisites. SVGFaith-Score significantly outperforms all nine baselines, including a Qwen3.5-122B-A10B judge, on Arena and in both Diagnostic directions. Code and data: https://github.com/Yukinonooo/SVGFaith.

title: Touch\'{e}World tech report : Towards Online Unified Camera--Hand Exploration in Generative Worlds
summary: Recent video world models allow users to explore generated environments through camera navigation. Continuous hand motion provides a fine-grained action channel for interacting with the people and objects encountered during exploration. We present Touch\'{e}World, a framework that integrates gesture-driven interaction into a camera-controlled video world model. Given an initial image and a scene-description prompt, the model generates video conditioned on temporally aligned camera and hand controls. We construct joint camera--hand training data from heterogeneous egocentric videos through annotation completion, consistency-based filtering, and temporal alignment. Building on a pretrained camera-controlled world model, we combine spatial hand-skeleton conditioning with numerical hand-motion features through parameter-efficient adaptation. Causal adaptation and few-step distillation support chunk-level online generation, allowing users to update their controls based on generated visual feedback. We further introduce Touch\'{e}Bench to evaluate hand-motion following, camera--hand coordination, online interaction, and object response. Together, these components establish a framework for studying continuous exploration and hand-driven interaction within generative worlds.

title: RouTex: Multi-reference 3D Texture Generation by Reprogramming Rotary Position Encoding
summary: While single-image 3D texture generation has advanced significantly, conditioning texture synthesis on multi-view reference images remains largely under-explored, despite its necessity for resolving surface ambiguity in unobserved regions. In this paper, we propose RouTex, a novel multi-reference 3D texture generation framework based on in-context Diffusion Transformers (DiT). Our key insight is that native 3D Rotary Position Encoding (RoPE) inherently possesses spatial addressing capabilities. We introduce Positional Routing (PR) to reprogram 3D RoPE along spatial and semantic dimensions, establishing explicit reference-to-view correspondence without introducing additional parameters. To execute this routing efficiently, Dual-Granularity Attention (DGA) combines per-view local attention for fine texture fidelity with global joint attention over deduplicated references for cross-view consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RouTex achieves new state-of-the-art performance in multi-reference 3D texture generation.

title: Jev with Foresight: Safe Language-Guided Autonomous Driving via a Language World Model
summary: Large language models understand passengers' driving commands, but as driving agents they reason in generated text for seconds and must infer each action's consequences implicitly from the scene. We present Jev-AD, which pairs Jev, a typed decision model that answers predefined questions with probabilities, not generated text, with a language world model that predicts for every candidate action how nearby vehicles move over the next two seconds. Code turns these predictions into foreseen consequences, which Jev compares instead of inferring them from coordinates. In simulated highway merging (500 car-episodes), this foresight lowers the same decision model's collision rate from 26.0% to 2.4% at 0.25 seconds per decision, and Jev-AD achieves the passenger's intent in 93% of free-form command trials. In 500 replayed real-world NGSIM episodes, foresight lowers the collision rate from 48.2% to 2.8%, and the world model, learned from this traffic, foresees 93% of dangerous actions. Project page: https://ys-qu.github.io/jev-ad-website.

title: Ctrl-F: Force as an Interface for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
summary: Humanoid motion tracking has scaled to general policies that reproduce diverse human motion, but the resulting behavior is in free-space: the tracker knows where the body should be, not how it should interact with the environment. Other work makes the object part of the objective, yet abstracts that interaction to contact or geometry, which leaves the demanding cases under-explored. We argue that force is a natural command channel between motion imitation and object interaction, one that specifies not just where to make contact but how hard. We present Ctrl-F, a hierarchical motion-force framework that augments motion tracking with an explicit force command, a 3-D force at each designated contact body such as a hand or a foot. The hierarchical framework comprises: (1) A unified motion-force controller tracks the reference motion while applying the commanded force to the world. (2) A high-level force planner that issues a force command online based on object state and proprioception observations. In simulation and on hardware, Ctrl-F completes loco-manipulation that demands large, sustained interaction force and adjusts its command online as the load changes, both out of reach of a force-blind tracker. On hardware, Ctrl-F demonstrates hand-based dragging, pushing, and lifting, as well as foot-based kicking, successfully manipulating boxes weighing up to 20kg in pushing and kicking tasks where the force-blind baseline fails, while adapting online to additional loads introduced mid-task.

title: MESA: An Evaluation Framework for Compositional, Semantic, and Spatial Generalization in Robotics
summary: Despite growing interest in foundation models for robotic manipulation, systematic evaluation of their capabilities remains elusive. Existing benchmarks are either narrow and saturated, offering little signal on SOTA methods, broadly scoped, providing diversity at the cost of controlled experimentation, or require training on large, messy open-source datasets. We introduce MESA, an evaluation framework designed for precise, reproducible measurement of language-conditioned policy generalization. MESA provides five evaluation suites that isolate in-distribution performance and four distinct axes of generalization: spatial configuration, object instance, object category, and subtask composition, enabling researchers to diagnose where and why policies fail, not just whether they fail. To populate these suites at scale, we develop MESA-Gen, a pipeline for task and demonstration generation built by improving MimicGen. We instantiate the framework on two platforms and release both: the single-arm MESA suite, and BiMESA, the first large-scale benchmark for bimanual generalization. We evaluate seven baseline methods spanning diffusion policies, VLM-based approaches, and pretrained VLAs, finding that the strongest model achieves only 52% on MESA and 49% on BiMESA, providing meaningful signal while leaving ample room for progress. MESA rankings are broadly consistent with RoboArena scores, suggesting that MESA captures method-level differences relevant beyond simulation. Project website: https://pairlab.github.io/MESA.

title: Contact-Implicit Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization for Dynamic Humanoid Locomotion on Parameterizable Uneven Terrain
summary: This letter presents a trajectory planner for humanoid robots to perform dynamic motions on complex, parameterizable terrains using a contact-implicit whole-body optimization framework. The planner generates feasible movements without predefined contact sequences, considering the robot's full dynamics and kinematics. To plan bipedal locomotion on steps, ramps, and other terrains, we propose a mathematical model to approximate ground geometry with a smooth surface. The rigid interaction between the robot and the ground is modeled via novel contact constraints, extending the domain of applicability from flat and horizontal surfaces to any arbitrary smooth surface. Effectiveness is demonstrated using nonlinear programming to plan motions on various terrain topologies. We also explore dynamic trajectory generation by embedding high-level requirements in the cost function and the initial guess. Preliminary feasibility tests were conducted over non-coplanar terrains, both in simulation and on the real robot ErgoCub.

title: Correct Robots Before They Make Mistakes: Proactive Human-in-the-Loop Intervention via Preference Learning
summary: This paper presents Proactive Human-in-the-Loop (PHIL), a framework for proactive policy correction and preference-based post-training. PHIL enables operators to preview policy-predicted future motion and intervene before anticipated undesirable actions. During takeover, PHIL continues querying the policy and displaying its predicted trajectories in the physical workspace through an extended reality (XR) interface. PHIL pairs rejected policy predictions with corrective action chunks subsequently executed from the same physical state over the same horizon, and preference-based post-training encourages the policy to favor these corrections. This paper evaluates PHIL on four real-world manipulation tasks using a diffusion policy and a pretrained vision-language-action policy. With five correction episodes per condition, PHIL increases mean success rates across the evaluated tasks and demonstration budgets from 44.0% to 70.3% for the diffusion policy and from 57.8% to 76.9% for X-VLA, compared with HG-DAgger. Separately, policies trained with proactive corrections show fewer unnecessary recovery behaviors in successful episodes. Project page: https://intuitive-robots.github.io/PHIL-page/.

title: OdorSpaces: Visual-Olfactory Embodied Navigation in 3D Environments
summary: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. We introduce OdorSpaces, a physics-based simulation platform and benchmark for visual-olfactory embodied navigation. OdorSpaces augments Habitat-Sim with 3D odor transport and dispersion simulated by Fire Dynamics Simulator (FDS), enabling agents to navigate photorealistic indoor environments using both visual and olfactory observations. The benchmark includes two representative source-seeking scenarios: invisible gas-leak localization and early-stage fire localization. We develop an initial multimodal reinforcement learning policy that integrates visual observations and olfactory measurements over time. Experiments show that the policy outperforms a diverse set of baselines, establishing a strong reference for future research on visual-olfactory embodied navigation.

title: GRASP: Gradient-Guided Sampling for Contact-Rich Physics-Based Motion Retargeting
summary: We study physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations for robot learning: finding robot controls that reproduce reference motions under contact dynamics. We propose GRASP (Gradient Recovery from Archived Samples for Proposals), which combines sampling-based exploration with gradient-guided refinement without requiring a differentiable simulator. GRASP-TO extends tempered sequential Monte Carlo by fitting local quadratic cost models to archived rollouts and using their gradients to guide Markov chain Monte Carlo rejuvenation. Metropolis-Hastings correction preserves the target distribution for each fixed proposal kernel, and a population analysis connects the recovered gradients to Gaussian smoothing. GRASP-MPC scales this optimizer to long demonstrations through warm-started receding-horizon planning. Experiments on dexterous hands and humanoids show accurate retargeting with a shared tracking objective and no task-specific contact rewards, including 92.8% success on 1352 bimanual OakInk2 demonstrations. The refined references improve PPO tracking in pen spinning and humanoid-object interaction. We also demonstrate dexterous manipulation and whole-body humanoid motion on real hardware.

title: Closed-Loop Adaptive Sampling on a Generative Ocean Model
summary: Adaptive sampling can substantially improve the value of sparse ocean observations by directing mobile robots toward measurements that are most informative for an evolving environment. Recent learned generative ocean models can produce high-resolution forecasts and ensembles at substantially lower computational cost than traditional numerical models, creating an opportunity to use rich predictive forecasts directly in closed-loop robotic sampling. However, these models do not natively provide the explicit uncertainty representations assumed by classical informative-planning methods, and their forecasts often evolve in learned latent spaces rather than directly in physical ocean variables. We develop a multi-robot closed-loop adaptive sampling framework that uses a single learned generative model for forecasting, uncertainty estimation, planning, and measurement assimilation. The model forecasts an ensemble in latent space, decodes it to physical ocean states, and uses ensemble statistics to construct A- or D-optimal sampling objectives. We select sampling locations subject to robot reachability under predicted currents. The collected measurements are assimilated back into the latent state using observation-conditioned diffusion sampling. Across 120 test scenarios A- and D-optimal sampling generally outperforms static, random, and systematic-coverage baselines while adding little planning overhead. Our experiments uncover several scenarios in which model uncertainty diverges from forecast error, motivating future work in uncertainty quantification.

title: ZipDrift: Generating Multimodal Short-Horizon MPC Costs with One-Step Drifting Models
summary: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert. We observe that the optimal correction is often multimodal: when a slower opponent can be passed on either side, good corrections of opposite sign coexist, and the expert's choice between them hinges on tiny cost differences. Deterministic regression then averages modes or inherits inconsistent expert tie-breaking. We propose ZipDrift, which trains a one-step drifting generator over MPC cost corrections, tilted toward low closed-loop cost and learned only from cost evaluations of candidate corrections, without differentiating through the optimiser. A few generated candidates are ranked by a learned critic, and the model-based MPC then enforces dynamics and constraints. In a kinematic overtaking benchmark derived from ZipMPC, 53% of contexts are bimodal and the manual short-horizon MPC crashes in 28.5% of test episodes. With an eight-dimensional stagewise correction, ZipDrift is collision-free in all 600 test episodes and matches the best evaluated candidate, whereas an idealised ZipMPC-style regressor crashes in 4.0% (16.0% with inconsistent expert labels) and critic-ranked random candidates with the same budget in 2.0%.

title: Diversity-Aware Experience Replay via Statistical Leverage Scores
summary: Off-policy deep reinforcement learning trains on random samples from a replay buffer of past experience. In physical robot settings, that buffer is dominated by routine: thousands of near-identical transitions from normal operation, while the rare events that define the edges of the task are rarely sampled. We propose scoring every stored transition by its statistical leverage, which measures how unusual it is relative to the buffer's own data, computed from the stored numbers alone, with no labels, rewards, or value network. We draw each mini-batch from a mixture of this score and uniform sampling. First, the natural way to build the score along the directions where the data varies most turns out to be blind when actions are stored as one-hot indicators, because indicator columns always win the variance ranking; we instead select the feature columns with the heaviest tails (largest kurtosis) where small far-away populations are revealed. Second, the importance weights that prioritized replay uses to keep gradients unbiased cancel the method exactly: with full correction, training matches uniform sampling, so we drop the correction and deliberately optimize the rebalanced objective. Third, when the rare situations of a log are relational, visible only in how a stretch of behavior relates to its goal, not in any single stored coordinate-per-transition scores are blind; applying the same tail rule to short trajectory windows described relative to their goal restores the signal, and on a three-joint arm that must push an object around an obstacle it raises the rare-task success from 0.49 to 0.69 against a labeled-oracle ceiling of 0.74.

title: LumiTac: Compact, High-Rate Six-Axis Optical Tactile Sensing for Human-Robot Interaction
summary: Integrating six-axis tactile feedback into robotic interfaces requires compact sensors with accurate load measurement and rapid online reconstruction. This paper presents LumiTac, a low-profile, camera-free optoelectronic tactile sensor combining spatially distributed illumination with spectral encoding. Five photoemitters and five RGBW photoreceivers are mounted on opposing circuit boards coupled through translucent silicone. Load-induced interlayer motion modulates the internal light field under compression, shear, bending, and torsion. The sensing head measures 12 mm in diameter and 4.75 mm in thickness, weighs less than 2 g, and has a component cost of approximately USD 7. A compact multilayer perceptron reconstructs three force and three moment components from 20 optical channels. Independent testing yielded coefficients of determination (R-squared) of 0.9657-0.9941, with mean absolute errors of 0.054-0.190 N for forces and 0.304-1.419 mN m for moments. Online prediction achieved an average update rate of 303.57 Hz and a median software processing latency of 0.722 ms. Experiments involving combined loading, light weights, and rapid tapping evaluated load tracking, sensitivity to small forces, and transient response, respectively. Robotic demonstrations further validated its applicability to tactile-guided manipulation and physical human-robot interaction.
