title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
summary: This paper explores how AI agents might direct their own evolution by modifying and evaluating their behavior, drawing parallels to Darwinian and Lamarckian adaptation.

title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration
summary: This research proposes a method for Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning using Epigraph-Form Guided Exploration to overcome challenges in discovering cooperative behaviors in complex joint state-action spaces.

title: When Verification Is Not Agreement: Cross-Agent LLM-to-Dafny Formalization
summary: This paper introduces a cross-agent formalization protocol where a Specifier model translates clinical trial criteria into a Dafny predicate, and an Impl model attempts to verify it, addressing when verification does not imply agreement.

title: Synthesizing symbolic models of human and machine reasoning at scale
summary: This research demonstrates how advances in artificial intelligence can scale the synthesis of symbolic models of human and machine reasoning, overcoming historical limitations of hand-engineering and computational tractability.

title: PromptOps: Iterative Prompt Optimization for LLM-as-a-Judge Systems
summary: This paper introduces PromptOps, an iterative prompt optimization method for large language model (LLM)-as-a-judge systems to maintain agreement with human evaluation policies despite changes in user interactions and score distributions.

title: Goal Revelation as a Bridge Between Information-Theoretic Empowerment and Capability-Based Human Power
summary: This paper explores 'Goal Revelation' as a formal, quantitative measure of power in AI agents, addressing concerns about AI safety, instrumental convergence, and potential human disempowerment.

title: Robust Ranking of Port Impacts from Impending Tropical Cyclones: A Two-Stage Recommendation System
summary: This paper proposes a two-stage recommendation system to robustly rank port impacts from impending tropical cyclones, aiding preparedness planning by anticipating affected ports and disruption durations.

title: EnvOpt: Automated Optimization for Agent Environments
summary: This paper introduces EnvOpt, a method for automated optimization of stationary environments for LLM agents, aiming to improve their cost-efficiency and success rates.

title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
summary: FINCOSMOS is presented as an open-world evaluation paradigm for language agents operating in the finance domain, designed to test their performance and trustworthiness with real-time web data and user strategies.

title: SAVeR$^2$: Reasoning-based Safety Alignment for Large Reasoning Models via Verifiable Rewards
summary: This paper introduces SAVeR$^2$, a reasoning-based safety alignment method for Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) that uses verifiable rewards to ensure non-malicious reasoning, safe answers, and safety consistency.

title: DelegateEval: Evaluating Platforms for Personal External Service Agents
summary: DelegateEval is introduced as a framework for evaluating platforms that host personal external service agents, which are AI agents managed by individuals to serve external clients.

title: Graph learning-assisted logic-based Benders decomposition for distributionally robust in-station train rescheduling under disruptions
summary: This paper develops a rolling-horizon distributionally robust model using graph learning and Benders decomposition for in-station train rescheduling, addressing uncertainty in resource reopening times during disruptions.

title: CST-Bench: Benchmarking Counterfactual Spatial Transition Reasoning with Causal Transition On-Policy Self-Distillation
summary: CST-Bench is introduced as a new benchmark to evaluate counterfactual spatial transition reasoning in multimodal large language models (MLLMs), focusing on how models infer scene state changes due to interventions.

title: FlashOffloading: Low-Latency KV Cache Offloading for Long-Context LLM Serving
summary: FlashOffloading is presented as a low-latency method for offloading the key-value (KV) cache from high-bandwidth memory (HBM) to host DRAM, addressing memory capacity limitations in long-context LLM serving systems.

title: Align Before Aggregation: Basis-Consistent Federated LoRA under Heterogeneous Ranks
summary: This paper proposes 'Align Before Aggregation', a method for basis-consistent federated low-rank adaptation (LoRA) that improves federated fine-tuning of LLMs under heterogeneous client capacities.

title: Embedding-Space Fingerprinting of LoRA Fine-Tunes: Recovering the Training-Data Domain from the Model Artifact Alone
summary: This paper studies whether a simple classifier can recover the training data domain of a LoRA fine-tuned model by analyzing only its weight deltas and internal activations. It investigates the extent of training data leakage into the model artifact.

title: Redacting Personal Data: A Speed and Accuracy Comparison of Regex, Presidio and Hybrid Designs
summary: This research compares the speed and accuracy of different methods, including Regex, Presidio, and hybrid designs, for redacting personally identifiable information (PII) from text before it is processed by large language models. The study aims to find efficient ways to protect sensitive data in enterprise LLM projects.

title: Don't Prompt Your Agents. Equip Them: Skillware as a Modular Standard for Sovereign, Auditable, and Deterministic Capability Execution for Logical Systems
summary: This paper introduces "Skillware" as a modular standard to equip autonomous logical systems, proposing a method for sovereign, auditable, and deterministic capability execution for agents. It aims to improve agent reliability and efficiency compared to dynamic code writing or extensive prompt engineering.

title: Who Should Know What? Empirical Information Design for Multi-Agent LLM Economies
summary: This research empirically investigates the impact of information-sharing policies on the performance of multi-agent large language model (LLM) systems. It explores how the level of detail provided to agents affects system outcomes.

title: MCPHallu: Benchmarking Reasoning, Execution, and Memory Hallucinations in MCP Agents
summary: This paper introduces MCPHallu, a new benchmark designed to evaluate reasoning, execution, and memory hallucinations in agents deployed through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It diagnoses failures in MCP agents beyond just task completion.

title: Towards Generalist Graph-Level Anomaly Detection
summary: This research proposes a new approach towards generalist graph-level anomaly detection (GLAD), aiming to overcome the limitations of existing dataset-specific methods that require substantial in-domain data and training.

title: Pediatric ECG foundation model via adult-to-pediatric fine-tuning: downstream tasks and clinical evaluation
summary: This study investigates adapting an adult ECG foundation model to pediatric electrocardiograms through fine-tuning, evaluating its performance on downstream tasks and in clinical settings. The goal is to improve AI interpretation of age-dependent pediatric ECGs.

title: RIVER: Evidence-guided multi-agent retrieval for enzyme--reaction discovery
summary: This paper introduces RIVER, an evidence-guided multi-agent retrieval system designed to assist in enzyme-reaction discovery. It aims to connect genomic information to biochemical reaction networks by identifying candidate enzymes.

title: The Intrusion Pathway: How Non-Evidential Context Degrades Language Model Performance
summary: This research investigates "The Intrusion Pathway," detailing how non-evidential context, such as irrelevant statements or random tokens, degrades language model accuracy. It highlights the impact of such noise in retrieval-augmented and long-context deployments.

title: Generate-then-Rank: Learning Symbolic Goal Interpretation for Embodied Agents
summary: This paper proposes a "Generate-then-Rank" method for embodied agents to interpret natural language instructions into formal symbolic goals, which is crucial for planning and action execution. This aims to improve how embodied AI translates human commands into executable plans.

title: FARR: Forecast-Aware Residual Refinement with Matched Endpoint Evidence for Long-Horizon Time-Series Forecasting
summary: This paper introduces FARR (Forecast-Aware Residual Refinement), a method designed to improve long-horizon time-series forecasting using large language models by refining auxiliary conditioning with matched endpoint evidence. It addresses how to prevent auxiliary information from increasing forecasting error.

title: Responsible GenAI Use During Active Armed Conflict: Evidence from Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms
summary: This research examines the use of Generative AI by community-based humanitarian responders in Sudan during active armed conflict, analyzing the challenges and conditions required for its responsible deployment in such critical environments.

title: When Bigger Becomes Brittle: Why Compression Hurts More as Language Models Scale
summary: This research investigates how compression techniques like quantization and pruning affect large language models as they scale, revealing that internal components are damaged more significantly than what output benchmark scores indicate.

title: GuidedWAM: Training-Free Energy Guidance for World Action Models in Autonomous Driving
summary: This paper introduces GuidedWAM, a training-free energy guidance mechanism for World Action Models (WAMs) in autonomous driving. This allows conditioning on new driving objectives without requiring model retraining.

title: Adaptive Semantic Branching: Disagreement-Localized Cross-Trajectory Regeneration for Reasoning Candidate Expansion
summary: This paper introduces Adaptive Semantic Branching (ASB), a training-free inference procedure that enhances reasoning by reusing alternative intermediate decisions from conflicting reasoning trajectories to explore new solutions.

title: How Finite Brains Generalize Without Bound: Spatial Memory as a Universal Computer
summary: This paper explores how finite brains generalize without bound, attributing this capacity to spatial memory functioning as a universal computer, contrasting this with the limitations of LSTMs and Transformers on longer sequences.

title: ChemE-as-Code: An Open-Source Platform for Agentic AI in Chemical Engineering
summary: ChemE-as-Code is an open-source platform that provides an environment for AI agents built on large language models to perform various chemical engineering tasks, including catalysis, process simulation, and plant layout.

title: Circe: Training-Free LLM Self-Evaluation via Component Interaction Consistency
summary: This paper introduces Circe, a training-free method for large language model (LLM) self-evaluation that assesses the correctness of responses via component interaction consistency, addressing the challenge of evaluating LLMs without reference answers.

title: A Behavioural Framework for Predicting and Understanding Loss of Control in Frontier Artificial Intelligence Systems
summary: This paper proposes a behavioral framework to predict and understand the risk of loss of control in frontier AI systems, where systems might operate beyond human oversight with potentially irreversible consequences.

title: TCSExam: Evaluating Frontier LLMs on the Full Range of TCS Research
summary: This paper introduces TCSExam, a unified framework and benchmark designed to evaluate frontier large language models on their capabilities across the full range of theoretical computer science research, including theorem proving and solver engineering.

title: Secure Formal Raising: Protecting the Development of AI through Executable Properties
summary: This paper proposes Secure Formal Raising (SFR), a framework that extends Formal Raising to model the security of AI development environments through explicit behavioral properties.

title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels
summary: This paper introduces DictLLM, a post-training compression technique for large language models using dictionary kernels, designed for efficient deployment on mobile devices.

title: MUSS: A Multi-scale and Sequence-based Model for Single-cell Gene Regulation
summary: This paper presents MUSS, a multi-scale and sequence-based model designed to jointly represent DNA sequence, chromatin accessibility, and gene expression for single-cell gene regulation studies.

title: Create Your Own Work Stack: Deploying Self-hosted AI and Tooling in a Tech Startup
summary: This article reports on the practical experience of a tech startup, Grayhat Developers, in deploying and managing a self-hosted, hybrid AI stack for their AI-intensive development workflow.

title: A Generative Foundation Model for Multimodal Tokamak Tasks
summary: This paper proposes a generative foundation model designed to handle diverse multimodal tasks within Tokamak experiments, including plasma reconstruction, evolution forecasting, and disruption risk estimation.

title: PCBRouteAgent: How Close Are LLM Agents to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers?
summary: This paper introduces PCBRouteAgent, an LLM-based agent designed to automate printed circuit board routing by coordinating connectivity decisions with geometric execution under design rules.

title: SMART: State-based Multi Agent Reasoning Traces for Verification-oriented Problem-Solving
summary: This paper proposes SMART, a multi-agent framework that uses state-based reasoning traces to gather knowledge and solve complex problems, particularly for verification-oriented tasks.

title: Signals, Evidence, and Context: User Scrutiny in Real-World LLM Conversations
summary: This study analyzes how users scrutinize, accept, check, and challenge LLM-generated answers based on features like supporting evidence in real-world conversations from ShareChat and WildChat.

title: Value-oriented policy distillation for interpretable wind farm power control
summary: This paper explores value-oriented policy distillation for interpretable control of wind farm power, aiming to help maintain system balance and prevent blackouts by adjusting power setpoints.

title: The Geometry of Simulated Perspectives: Dissociating Representation and Behaviour in a Multimodal Language Model
summary: This research investigates how assigning different perspectives to a multimodal language model reshapes its internal representations and influences its judgments, focusing on visual interestingness.

title: LeanContext: Disentangling Mathematical Resources from Local Formal Context in Lean Whole-Proof Generation
summary: This paper introduces LeanContext, a method for disentangling mathematical resources from local formal context to improve whole-proof generation in neural theorem proving.

title: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated, Physics-Informed Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization and Calibrated Uncertainty
summary: This paper presents SteelAgent, an LLM-orchestrated system that combines metallurgical descriptors and machine learning models for physics-informed steel property prediction, uncertainty reporting, and inverse design.

title: Octopus: One Brain, Many Branches for Latent-KV Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper introduces Octopus, a novel architecture for multi-agent reinforcement learning in LLM systems that optimizes latent-KV cache management to avoid duplication across parallel exploration branches.

title: Big Models, Small Gains: Frozen Forecasters as Classifiers on MONSTER
summary: This paper evaluates whether forecasting foundation models, used as frozen feature extractors, provide a significant advantage over traditional classifiers for time series classification on the MONSTER dataset.

title: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time
summary: This paper introduces LowRAM, a method for composable KV cache compression at test-time for autoregressive decoding, utilizing low-rank keys and amortized values to reduce memory footprint.

title: Stochastic Dynamics of Generative AI: From Autoregressive Models to Interacting LLM Networks and Neural SDEs
summary: This paper develops a stochastic dynamical-systems perspective on generative AI models, formulating LLMs as high-dimensional nonlinear autoregressive models and connecting them to neural stochastic differential equations.

title: Finite-Time Convergence and Regret Guarantees for Neural Reinforcement Learning in POMDPs
summary: This paper presents finite-time convergence and regret guarantees for neural reinforcement learning algorithms operating in Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs).

title: Shaping & Monitoring Models through their Internal Representations
summary: This paper proposes Mechanistic Shaping, a unified framework to guide and monitor AI models during training by directly influencing their internal representations to adhere to specific behavioral rules.

title: Server-Side Sparse Assignment for Federated Mixture-of-Experts
summary: This paper introduces server-side sparse assignment for federated Mixture-of-Experts, aiming to improve collaborative fine-tuning of large language models on heterogeneous edge devices.

title: A Night at the LLM Zoo: Data Conditioned Flow Matching for Generating Pretrained LLM Weights
summary: This paper presents a method using data-conditioned flow matching to generate pretrained LLM weights, creating an 'LLM Zoo' to advance Weight Space Learning for large language models.

title: Regulating Autonomous Mobility-on-Demand Operators with Fixed and Adaptive Penalties: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
summary: This paper studies how penalty-based regulation can limit profit-maximizing autonomous mobility-on-demand operators from exploiting consumers or underserving regions. It uses a multi-agent reinforcement learning approach to model the system.

title: Machine Learning for Live-Birth Prediction After IVF/ICSI From Structured Clinical Data: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Critical Appraisal
summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates machine-learning models used for predicting live birth after IVF or ICSI from routine clinical data. It assesses their reported performance and methodology.

title: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification for Cancer Histopathology: Calibrated Uncertainty Under Distribution Shift
summary: This research focuses on improving the reliability of cancer diagnosis models by proposing a scalable Bayesian Gaussian process classification method that provides calibrated uncertainty under distribution shifts. This is crucial for clinical deployment.

title: Teaching Agents the "Principle", Not the "Reward"
summary: This paper argues that teaching reinforcement learning agents underlying 'principles' rather than just relying on reward signals can help them learn more generalizable policies in complex tasks.

title: Depth or Description? When a One-Step Latent Score Replaces Lookahead in Proactive Information Acquisition
summary: This research investigates whether a simpler one-step latent score can effectively replace expensive lookahead computations for proactive agents deciding what information to acquire before acting. It highlights the importance of how hidden causes are described.

title: A Survey of Nonlinear Filtering Methods for Data Assimilation and Recent Advances in Generative AI-Enabled Score Filters
summary: This survey reviews nonlinear filtering methods for data assimilation in complex dynamical systems, highlighting recent advances in generative AI-enabled score filters for applications like weather prediction and wildfire tracking.

title: Backbone-Informed Adaptation after EEG Pretraining: A Capacity-Controlled Study
summary: This study investigates the effectiveness of backbone-informed adapters for Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models during downstream learning, comparing their performance against other adapter designs.

title: TrustMix: Graceful Degradation for Pretrained Models under Distribution Shift
summary: TrustMix is proposed as a lightweight post-hoc method to enable pretrained models to degrade gracefully under distribution shifts by making their extrapolation assumptions explicit.

title: Structured Machine Theory of Mind from Agent Trajectories
summary: This research aims to develop predictive models of human behavior that represent underlying mental states, allowing for principled interventions rather than just statistical prediction from trajectory data.

title: Canonical Correlation Neural Networks
summary: This paper introduces Canonical Correlation Neural Networks, which use the covariance matrix as a principled substitute for known structures to provide relational inductive biases when explicit structure is unavailable.

title: Fractional physics-informed neural networks to model social media virality
summary: This research presents a fractional physics-informed neural network designed to model social media virality by learning both the temporal memory and nonlinear growth dynamics of engagement.

title: Compositional Unalignment: Auditing Safety in Large Vision-Language Models
summary: This paper addresses the vulnerability of large vision-language models to compositional harm, where benign inputs become harmful when combined, and discusses the challenges of auditing this safety aspect.

title: TileQuant: Tile as the Precision-Allocation Unit for LLM Mixed-Precision Post-Training Quantization
summary: TileQuant is proposed as a post-training quantization method for LLMs that uses tiles as precision-allocation units to reduce deployment costs while preserving model quality by accounting for uneven weight sensitivity.

title: Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers
summary: This paper introduces the Loopback Transformer, offering a unified view of residual looped transformers by analyzing how representations are stored and reused after repeated application of shared blocks.

title: Neural Compression over Equivalence Classes: Exact Gauges and Functional Rate-Distortion
summary: This research explores using the representational freedom of neural networks—where many parameterizations yield similar functions—for compression, rather than redesigning codecs.

title: MAC-v2: Long-horizon model-based value expansion from pixels
summary: This paper investigates the effectiveness of long-horizon model-based value expansion as a framework for pixel-based offline reinforcement learning, a task that requires learning both representations and long-term values.

title: KG-Neighbor: Knowledge-Guided Neighborhood Construction for Embedding Visualization
summary: KG-Neighbor proposes a method for knowledge-guided neighborhood construction to improve embedding visualizations, ensuring that derived neighborhoods accurately reflect semantic relationships.

title: Using Transformers for Teaching and Learning via Symbolic Distillation of Neural A-life Agents
summary: This research explores using Transformers for symbolic distillation of neural A-life agents to make their evolved behaviors more interpretable and transferable between different neural architectures.

title: TriAttention: Unified Sparse Mixed-Precision Attention for Long-Context LLM Inference
summary: TriAttention introduces a unified sparse mixed-precision attention mechanism designed to optimize long-context LLM inference by selectively skipping interactions and adjusting precision based on individual interaction requirements.

title: Reweighting is not Harmless: Understanding the Role of Dataset Characteristics
summary: This paper analyzes the impact of reweighting, a common pre-processing method for fairness, arguing that it is not always harmless and its effects depend significantly on dataset characteristics.

title: Energy Measurement and Optimization of TinyML in Resource-Constrained Embedded Systems: A Systematic Mapping Study
summary: This paper presents a systematic study on measuring and optimizing energy consumption for TinyML in resource-constrained embedded systems, relevant for IoT applications.

title: How Deep is the Signal? Time-Context up to 30 Years for Colorectal Cancer Prediction in a Primary-Care EHR Model
summary: This research investigates the optimal 'time-context' up to 30 years for EHR foundation models to predict colorectal cancer, analyzing how far back in time medical data provides predictive signals.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Resource Allocation in Integrated Sensing and Communication
summary: This paper explores the application of Graph Neural Networks for optimizing resource allocation in vehicular integrated sensing and communication networks, balancing sensing and communication demands.

title: Scenario Augmentation for Rare Financial Events via Multimodal Latent Diffusion
summary: This study examines the use of multimodal latent diffusion models for generating synthetic scenarios to augment data for rare financial events, aiming to improve their representation and classification.

title: How do Transformers Perform Low-Level Control In-Context?
summary: This research investigates how Transformer-based neural networks perform low-level control tasks using their in-context learning abilities, by analyzing system evolution data.

title: WeightLoop: Weight-Space Programming with Experimental Feedback
summary: This paper introduces WeightLoop, a method where language models engage in weight-space programming to reason about and rewrite neural network weights, using experimental feedback for recursive self-improvement.

title: Rethinking Data Selection: The Importance of Coverage over Difficulty in LLM Fine-Tuning
summary: This research re-evaluates data selection strategies for LLM fine-tuning, proposing that data coverage is more important than difficulty for reducing computational costs.

title: Permanent and Transient Representations for Continual Reinforcement Learning
summary: This paper proposes using permanent and transient representations to address the stability-plasticity trade-off in Continual Reinforcement Learning, allowing agents to adapt while retaining prior knowledge.

title: AtlasULP: Domain-aware Universal Link Prediction via Relation Atlas
summary: This paper introduces AtlasULP, a domain-aware approach for universal link prediction in graph learning, aiming to overcome the limitations of dataset-specific training.

title: Test-Time Self-Play: Scaling without a Verifier
summary: This research proposes a 'Test-Time Self-Play' method to scale large language model performance at deployment without relying on an external verifier to score solutions.

title: When Scores Conflict with Preferences: Pre-Alignment Diagnosis and Adaptive Correction of Constraint Drift in DPO
summary: This paper addresses conflicts between pairwise preferences and pointwise criteria in Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), proposing methods for diagnosis and adaptive correction of constraint drift.

title: Spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant representations
summary: This theoretical work explores how symmetry imposes rank constraints on equivariant representations in geometric deep learning, revealing spectral symmetry fingerprints in equivariant graph neural networks.

title: IMUDINO: Self-distilled Foundation Model for Inertial Sensing
summary: IMUDINO is presented as the first self-distilled foundation model for inertial sensing, demonstrating competitive performance across diverse tasks like human activity recognition, motion capture, and odometry.

title: Two-stage residual learning for calibrated uncertainty in solar irradiance forecasts
summary: This paper introduces a two-stage residual learning approach to achieve calibrated uncertainty estimates in solar irradiance forecasts, improving the reliability of renewable generation predictions.

title: Echoes of Error: Residual-Directional Local Rollout Consistency for Timeseries Forecasting
summary: This research formalizes the impact of rollout errors in time-series forecasting through 'local rollout consistency,' proposing a method to mitigate how initial errors perturb future predictions.

title: Adversarial Robustness of Kernel Machines: A Comprehensive Analysis
summary: This paper provides a comprehensive empirical investigation into the adversarial robustness of kernel machines, analyzing their susceptibility to adversarial examples.

title: Localization Does Not Imply Steerability: A Mechanistic Study of Sign Errors in LLM Mathematics
summary: This mechanistic study investigates characteristic sign errors in large language models during multi-step mathematical computations, demonstrating that localization of errors does not imply steerability.

title: Learning Multi-Agent Orchestration:Higher-Order Interactions in Policy Improvement
summary: This research explores learning orchestration for LLM-based multi-agent systems, focusing on how higher-order interactions can improve policy in such systems.

title: RLGPA: A Reinforcement Learning-Guided Granularity Planning Attack for Decision-Based Sparse Adversarial Examples
summary: This paper proposes RLGPA, a reinforcement learning-guided method for generating decision-based sparse adversarial examples by dynamically adjusting perturbation granularity.

title: Ranní výběr: Strach z omezení AI a datových center v USA táhne trhy dolů
summary: Morning Selection: Fear of potential restrictions on AI and data centers in the US is causing markets to decline.

title: Interactive Backdoor Attacks in LLM-Based Proactive Dialogue Systems
summary: LLM-based proactive dialogue systems provide goal-directed support through sustained interaction. Fine-tuning their underlying models on externally supplied dialogue data introduces backdoor risks. Existing LLM backdoor studies primarily focus on eliciting an attacker-specified response upon trigger activation. We present an interactive backdoor attack framework that uses training-data poisoning to steer post-trigger, multi-turn interactions toward an attacker-specified objective. Poisoned fine-tuning dialogues implant a trigger-conditioned guidance-policy bias that ordinary user utterances can activate, without deployment-time prompt modification or further attacker intervention. Specifically, we instantiate three complementary attacks under progressively expanded post-trigger interaction settings: (1) Direct Attack, which targets an immediate response deviation upon trigger activation, retaining the conventional trigger--response setting; (2) Constrained Progressive Attack, which progressively advances the attack objective along a predefined multi-turn trajectory; and (3) Unconstrained Progressive Attack, which extends target-directed steering to open-ended interactions with varied user continuations. Using psychological counseling as a representative setting, experiments on two LLM backbones and two dialogue datasets show that all three attacks effectively achieve their objectives under their respective interaction settings while largely preserving normal utility. Separate defense evaluations show that the tested training-data filters retain nearly all poisoned dialogues, while three post-admission baselines leave substantial residual attack-specific success.

title: On the Opportunities and Challenges of Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-Model Transfer
summary: Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-model Transfer (PACT), a form of latent communication between language models, combines a larger model's prompt representations with a smaller model's efficient generation, offering a promising way to balance capability and inference cost. However, existing systems provide limited support for independently evaluating large-small model collaboration, and improved task performance alone does not establish whether the receiver benefits from the sender's information. We introduce PLatour, an open-source PACT framework that connects frozen models through lightweight, zero-initialized linear bridges trained directly with task rewards and supports hybrid-attention architectures. PLatour significantly outperforms open-source baselines on generation tasks and surpasses Mostik's reported results on shared mathematics and coding benchmarks using a substantially smaller sender. However, controlled experiments show that the gains on some tasks can be reproduced by uninformative sender signals, self-communication, or receiver-only training. We find that trainable bridges can act as parameter-efficient adaptation mechanisms without exploiting useful sender information. We therefore propose PACT-Check to quantify how much of a trained PACT system's gain genuinely comes from communication. Finally, we discuss the opportunities and challenges of PACT systems. Code is available at https://github.com/zhenyi4/platour.

title: Reclassification Is All You Missed: Surfacing Variant Reinterpretation Need in Online Health Communities at Population Scale
summary: Genetic variants are routinely reclassified in ClinVar after a patient is tested, sometimes from uncertain to pathogenic, yet patient recontact is inconsistent, with no clear duty and responsibility diffused among labs, providers, and patients. Many affected people discuss their results in public online health communities that clinical recontact often does not reach. We built PRISM, an agentic large-language-model pipeline that screens these posts, checks whether the variant was later reclassified, and drafts a disclaimer-bearing outreach message, in a no-contact dry run. Across 3.9 million posts from 32 communities, agent-predicted reinterpretation-relevant discussion is rare (0.288%) but concentrated in specialist genetics communities (6.30% versus 0.10% in general medical-advice communities) and growing fivefold since 2014; PRISM surfaces 123 candidate classification differences, 5 of them from an uncertain submission to pathogenic or likely pathogenic. On a held-out set of 30 real-post drafts, a clinician judged 27 factually grounded and 15 fit to send: factual accuracy is necessary but not sufficient for clinically acceptable outreach. PRISM contributes a population-scale reinterpretation-need map with code and data to be released upon publication.

title: Adapting LLM Judges to Observed Human Annotation Policy through Soft Prompt Tuning
summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly employed as automated judges for evaluating chatbot responses. While proprietary models can achieve high agreement with human annotators, they remain costly and difficult to deploy in practical settings. Lightweight open-source LLM judges provide an attractive alternative but typically exhibit lower agreement with human ratings. In this paper, we investigate whether soft prompt tuning can align open-source LLM judges more closely with human annotation policy. We train soft prompts on the FairBotBench benchmark and evaluate the adapted judges across the dimensions of bias, toxicity, and personalization. Our findings demonstrate that hybrid soft-prompt tuning, which combines textual prompts with learned continuous prompt embeddings, consistently improves agreement with human annotations over the corresponding untuned baselines. For Qwen 3.5 9B, the adapted judges surpass both hosted reference judges across all three evaluation dimensions.

title: Matriarchy Classics: A Computational Approach to Swap Only Gendered Words in Classic Novels
summary: This paper proposes a trustworthy computational method to gender-swap public domain novels, with programmatic guarantees that only gendered words are inverted and all other words are left unchanged. This may seem like a simple task, but both large language models and naive rule-based methods fail to complete it. The proposed method includes a custom whitespace-preserving tokenizer, gender-swap mappings across plural and possessive forms, pronoun handling, and a character renaming strategy. It shortens the time required to gender-swap a novel from weeks of manual labor to minutes. The method is demonstrated on two public-domain novels. Pride and Prejudice is transported to matriarchal Regency England, where inheritance flows through daughters, mothers rule the household, and a frantic Mr. Bennet is determined to secure advantageous marriages for his sons. The Great Gatsby pivots to a matriarchal Jazz Age where newly-rich Ms. Gatsbee throws lavish parties in the hopes of reuniting with her lost love, David, who is now married to the violent Thelma Buchanan. Gender-swapped novels could serve as useful tools to investigate the gender biases of readers, authors, societies, and AI systems.

title: SAFE-Teen: Evaluating Chatbot Safety Across Adolescent Mental Health Conversations
summary: Adolescents are increasingly turning to AI chatbots for mental health support, advice, and companionship, raising safety concerns. While recent evaluations have started to examine safety across multiple conversational turns, few compare how slight changes in a teen's responses can affect a chatbot's safety in the same scenario. We conduct a clinician-informed evaluation of chatbot safety in simulated conversations with adolescents aged 13-17, examining how safety failures vary with adolescents' responses and teen-aware system prompting. We evaluated 32,555 simulated conversations across 18 chatbot APIs and two system-prompt conditions using 22 safety criteria grounded in previously identified harms. Conversations spanned 983 variants of 106 seed scenarios covering urgent safety issues, health advice, and identity and relationships. The overall criterion failure rate was 43.3% without the teen-aware prompt and 24.9% with it. The teen-aware prompt reduced failures, but it didn't eliminate them. When a teenager pushed back on a chatbot's answer, failures on mental health diagnosis, medication, and substance misuse boundaries rose by 10-12 percentage points without the prompt, for more than 80% of chatbots. These findings reveal persistent safety failures in simulated adolescent-chatbot interactions and show that safety depends on how a conversation unfolds.

title: Source-balanced Capped Fisher: Bounded Evidence Aggregation for User Inference in Language Models
summary: User inference asks whether a source contributed documents to a language-model update, even when the auditor observes only fresh documents from that source. Document-level scores can provide evidence of participation, but combining this evidence is challenging: documents differ in baseline predictability and in how strongly they reflect information learned from other documents of the same source. We propose source-balanced capped Fisher (SCF), an aggregation method that uses known nonparticipating sources to assess how unusual each document score is. It transforms the resulting reference-tail frequencies into negative-log evidence, caps individual contributions, and averages them within each source. This limits the influence of isolated extreme scores while retaining evidence across multiple documents. We complete the inference procedure with a decision rule that tests source participation using a p-value calibrated against a separate set of known nonparticipating sources. The rule provides finite-sample Type-I error control under source exchangeability. Experiments across four real-world datasets show that SCF achieves the highest AUROC among the evaluated aggregation methods in four domains. With the calibration-based decision rule, SCF delivers consistently competitive detection power across the tested settings, achieving the highest power in many cases, while empirical false-positive rates remain generally close to or below the nominal levels.

title: Recursive Sparse Attention: Million-Token Length Extrapolation at Logarithmic Cost
summary: At context lengths of about 1M tokens, dense attention is costly in prefill and decoding, and training typically relies on long documents, which become scarcer as the target length increases. Most sparse attention methods score all preceding blocks or tokens, so their selection cost per query is $O(L)$ at context length $L$; hierarchical selection reduces it to $O(\log L)$, but prior trainable hierarchical methods report accuracy only within their training length. We propose RecSA (Recursive Sparse Attention), which builds a tree over the KV cache in which each node summarizes its subtree with one key and one mean-pooled value. The keys come from one pooler per layer, shared by all levels and distilled from dense attention. Each level above the tokens selects at most $k$ candidates, so each query has $O(\log L)$ selection cost and reads $O(\log L)$ entries; the summaries of unselected candidates share one softmax with the exact tokens. Each entry's RoPE position is its index among the candidates of its level, so at any length every relative distance stays within the range seen during training. Initialized from Qwen3-4B and trained on 0.62B tokens at the original model's 32K training length, RecSA outperforms all baselines on RULER at every length from 131K to 2M; at 1M, it scores 60.5, compared with 40.0 for the best baseline, Dense + DCA. With our optimized kernels, RecSA is faster than dense attention in end-to-end prefill and decoding from 64K to 2M; at 524K on one H200 GPU, it accelerates prefill by 3.2x and decoding by 3.8x.

title: Archetypal contexts in the neurons of language models: an architecture for intelligence?
summary: We validate our previous hypothesis that a language model holds relational patterns apart from the subject domains that instantiate them (Nordfors, 2026). These archetypal contexts are patterns of relations that people recognize across many fields, such as the tipping point or winner takes all, held once and applied across domains. We show this inside the model, Qwen3.8-27B. One set of neurons carries the archetype, say the tipping point; another carries the topic, say politics, ecology or cell biology; a third carries the language, such as English, Spanish or Chinese. Silence the tipping point's neurons, and the model no longer identifies the pattern but still knows what the text is about. Silence the topic's, and it loses the topic but still names the pattern. In the neuron maps the layers organize themselves into a sandwich: the outer layers carry languages, the layers inside them topics, the layers at the heart archetypes. The sandwich emerges spontaneously during pretraining and appears in every model we mapped. Archetypes are the architecture for analogy, and we strongly suggest that this structure of archetypes and topics is the mechanism of a language model's intelligence: we see it self-organize as the model is trained. The neurons, the texts and the code are released with this paper as its reproduction package, so that anyone can repeat the test inside the model.

title: How Do AI Agents Waste Your Money?
summary: AI agents may consume massive tokens across a wide range of tasks, but how many of those tokens are really necessary? Although prior work has shown that agents can incur unexpectedly high token costs, we still lack a systematic way to identify and measure token waste. In this work, we introduce a unified framework for measuring token waste across heterogeneous agent systems. Our framework records and normalizes complete agent trajectories, identifies removable spans using an LLM-as-a-Judge (LLMaJ), and maps the identified text spans back to the original trajectory for token-level measurement. We validate the identified waste through direct interventions by removing marked spans, resuming agent execution, and measuring changes in task outcomes and subsequent actions. In online pruning experiments, we remove 41-46% of the model's reasoning while largely preserving task performance across two distinct agent benchmarks. Using this framework, we analyze agents across multiple settings. Our analysis shows that token waste has a system-level structure that aggregate token usage alone cannot reveal. First, waste varies more across tasks and agent settings than across models. Second, reasoning and visible execution can exhibit different waste patterns. Third, different harnesses can introduce distinct sources of inefficiency even under the same model and task. Overall, our framework transforms token waste into an actionable optimization signal, enabling researchers and practitioners to train more efficient models, design better reasoning strategies, and optimize agent harnesses toward reducing unnecessary computation rather than merely reducing token usage.

title: Encoding and Propagation of Grammatical Number in Large Language Models
summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) have become an increasingly popular means of translating Large Language Model (LLM) hidden state vectors into a human-comprehensible list of features or symbols. As such, SAEs may provide insight into an LLM's knowledge representation and internal ``mental'' grammar - topics of pragmatic interest for mechanistic interpretation of AI behavior and of theoretical interest for the study of in silico representations of human language. Language models with fewer than 100M parameters, trained on small corpora, nonetheless exhibit strong grammatical competence and discourse coherence, despite producing content of limited reliability. We use SAEs that we trained on one such model (Pythia-70M) to conduct an in-depth examination of how a single grammatical phenomenon, number agreement, is represented and processed in an LLM. We demonstrate the mechanism and the methodology by which SAEs can be used to find and propagate ``plural noun'', ``plural matrix subject'', and ``generate a plural verb'' features which cause the LLM to produce plural verb forms such as ``are'', ``do'', or ``have'' instead of ``is'', ``does'', and ``has'' in response to prompts such as ``the men in the park''. We show that intervening to remove these features from the hidden states of plural subject noun tokens causes the model to produce singular verbs instead, and vice versa. We also show that corresponding ``singular noun'' and ``generate a singular verb'' features are not as effective for this task. This asymmetry suggests that Pythia-70m makes use of a privative representation of grammatical number in English. These findings replicated with larger LLMs Gemma-2-2b and Llama-3.1-8b yielded similar results. Our main contribution is a novel approach to the use of SAEs to understanding how LLMs encode human language that addresses a number of technical and methodological challenges.

title: Latency-Aware Adaptive Best-of-$N$
summary: Test-time compute (TTC) improves language model responses by spending additional computation at inference time, and the right amount of compute depends on the prompt. Adaptive TTC methods allocate compute based on signals of response quality such as observed rewards, often by stopping once the signal exceeds a fixed threshold, and generally measure cost by the number of generations or tokens. But in online serving, latency is also a cost: it grows with server load, so a method using a fixed threshold spends too little compute when generation is fast and too much when it is slow. For Best-of-$N$ sampling, a widely used TTC method, we propose a two-stage adaptive algorithm that draws an initial batch, then uses the observed rewards and the batch's latency to decide whether to draw a second batch and at what size by comparing expected improvement against predicted cost: it draws one when the first batch's best reward is below a threshold that decreases with the first batch's latency, without explicitly measuring server load. We map each reward to its value under the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of the prompt's reward distribution, so the same tradeoff parameters can be reused across tasks; a regression fitted offline on other prompts predicts a distribution for the CDF value of the first batch's best reward, giving the expected improvement in closed form. We evaluate the method by simulation on a preference-based alignment benchmark, measuring generations-equivalent cost: generations plus latency, converted to generations. The method reaches Best-of-$N$'s reward at lower generations-equivalent cost, and conditioning on the measured first-batch latency saves at least as much of that cost as fixed-threshold (latency-unaware) baselines, and more when latency is highly variable, when it grows with batch size, and when the second batch's latency is highly predictable from the first's.

title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
summary: How can an agent handle a real-world task end to end? Frontier models with their own harnesses still fall short on real-world benchmarks: on Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex resolves 37.3% of the tasks and Claude Opus 5 with Claude Code 51.8%. These tasks fail at the step from reaching a resource to applying it, which we call the last mile to the real world. Existing approaches put the resource within reach but leave the competence to apply it with the caller, so each harness rebuilds that competence. We introduce agent-native primitives, reusable units that equip a resource with a resident LLM that applies it in context and communicates with other primitives, and HEELO (Harness Engineering around Evolving Agent-Native Primitives for the Last Mile to Real-WOrld Tasks), a harness engineering framework that builds each task's harness from a library of such primitives. HEELO composes the primitives a task needs into a task-specific graph, verifies the result against evidence from the environment, revises the primitives a failure implicates, and admits new or improved primitives after validation. We instantiate HEELO with eight primitive families, each built for one kind of task, and evaluate them on more than twenty benchmarks. Dev-Primitives raise Terminal-Bench 4.0 resolution from 37.3% under Codex to 55.5% on the same backbone, Harness Primitives composed per task raise Terminal-Bench 2.0 Pass@1 from 60.0% for the seed harness to 72.2%, Tool Primitives raise ToolBench pass rate from 55.8% to 75.1%, and Navigation Primitives raise GAIA-Text-103 accuracy from 45.6% to 58.3%. On the 46 real-world tasks of our heelo.dev platform, Claude Opus 5.5 with Claude Code and GPT-6.1 Sol with Codex complete 9 each on their own and 39 and 35 when connected to HEELO through our MCP server, with 1.9$\times$ and 2.3$\times$ less time and 1.55$\times$ lower cost per completed task.

title: ReviewMap: Mapping Evaluative Acts and Automation Boundaries in Peer-Review Comments
summary: Peer-review comments check what a paper does and judge why it matters, but no existing scheme distinguishes these two evaluative acts. We argue that making these acts explicit and measuring how reliably LLMs identify them is a prerequisite for responsible LLM-assisted review analysis: humans need to inspect review judgments and their grounds. This defines a more honest mission for NLP in peer review than full automation. We present ReviewMap, a framework that classifies each comment as assessment of claims and scholarly standards or calibration of contribution value and venue fit, with finer-grained attributes applied conditionally by act type. Applied to 500 ICLR~2026 papers through multi-model LLM consensus, the act layer proves reliably automatable under the operational guideline (inter-model $\kappa \geq 0.75$), supported by five-human validation on 470 development comments, while the attribute layer requires human oversight, defining a measured automation boundary. At the corpus level, 17% of reviewer-paper instances contain no panel-coded calibration, and the panel-coded calibration share is nearly $3\times$ as high in Strengths as in Weaknesses. This boundary informs three affordances: a review guideline that operationalizes the assessment-then-calibration workflow for reviewers, a per-comment rebuttal strategy scaffold for authors, and a discussion-phase dashboard for area chairs.

title: Enhancing Repository-Level Code Completion with Reinforcement Learning in Real-World Scenarios
summary: The rapid development of large language models (LLMs) for code, which closely aligns with the practical needs of real-world software development, has sparked growing attention in repository-level code completion. However, existing Code LLMs present challenges in focusing on suitable contexts from the repository and in deeply reasoning about cross-file dependencies. To address these challenges, we propose a novel reinforcement learning framework for repository-level code completion. To better understand both in-file and cross-file contexts, we employ identifier-driven intent recognition to capture completion intent, thereby improving the model's performance in real-world scenarios. To enhance cross-file reasoning, we propose a reward-driven completion learning to effectively reward in complex repository completion scenarios. To guide LLMs in completing code that aligns with intended functionality and repository context, we introduce a selective-exploration strategy that directs the model to focus on low-confidence, high-reward tokens, promoting the exploration of valuable, underexplored completion patterns. Experimental results show that our approach significantly improves the performance of Code LLMs. The code and the dataset are available at https://github.com/zhenlongDai/RepoCompletion.

title: The Memory Trap: Language Agents Overgeneralize from Benign Interactions
summary: Language agents increasingly use persistent memory to record user preferences and procedures across sessions. We show that memory from benign interactions can cause unsafe or unreliable behavior on later tasks. We call this failure the memory trap. To study this issue, we compare behavior in sessions with and without memory across six frontier models (including Claude Sonnet, Opus, and Fable models and GPT-5.6). We evaluate these models in a range of settings. First, in autonomy experiments, we find that requests to skip confirmation during low-stakes coding chores lead agents to skip confirmation and verification on simulated high-stakes tasks in both coding and everyday life. We next study memories formed when users seek emotional support, or describe harm from uncritical feedback, and find these memories bias later judgments of mathematical work, arguments, and poems toward sycophancy or over-critique (respectively). Memory notes written during legitimate stale-test repairs lead agents to weaken correct tests that catch broken safeguards; these memories also increase cheating on ImpossibleBench, with larger increases for stronger Sonnet and Opus models. We show that memory traps can arise both from overgeneralizations in memory writing, and when acting on memory. These findings demonstrate that even benign interactions can lead to serious risks from memory systems, and thus motivate the need for new research into ensuring that agents preserve the scope of their memories.

title: SKIM: Pruning Large Language Model Agents via Selective Knowledge Informed Masking
summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed under structured generation, where grammar constraints enforce output format at inference time. Whereas existing compression methods target unconstrained generation, we first identify a fundamental mismatch: under structured generation, grammar constraints reduce the model's output distribution to valid tokens, and the logits matter most at the small set of positions that decide the agent's action. Motivated by this finding, we propose SKIM (Selective Knowledge-Informed Masking), the first pruning and distillation framework for LLM agents under structured generation, with both stages guided by token role. SKIM partitions token positions into context, decision, and format categories, and this partition drives two complementary axes: (1) category-aware pruning saliency scores that preserve parameters most relevant for decision positions; and (2) an on-policy distillation objective that aligns student and teacher on valid tokens, paired with category-aware feature matching. We evaluate SKIM on tool-calling benchmarks and within multi-step agent loops, across multiple model scales and sparsity levels. SKIM consistently improves accuracy over baselines, with its superiority becoming most striking in high-sparsity regimes where conventional methods struggle, demonstrating the potential of category-aware compression for deployment-time grammar-constrained agents.

title: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Against Covert Misalignment
summary: As LLM agents advance rapidly in autonomy, the risk of hidden objectives that bypass safety constraints becomes increasingly plausible. Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring offers a key control mechanism by reading the agent's reasoning and flagging misalignment before it materializes into action, yet its reliability depends on the realism of the red-team it is stress-tested against. Existing red-teaming efforts rely on shared templates, such as casting a side task as a prerequisite, which treat the side objective as an exogenous insertion and leave task-specific, contextually grounded evasions underexplored. We therefore ask: How robust is CoT monitoring against agents that strategically conceal misalignment? To answer this, we introduce TraceMRT, an automated Trace-level Monitor Red-Teaming framework that reframes the side task as a coherent sub-goal of the primary task and searches trace-shaping strategies whose induced trajectories complete the misaligned objective while reading as natural execution. Through black-box attacks on state-of-the-art monitors such as GPT-5.2 and Claude-4.5, we reveal substantial vulnerabilities even in top models. To counter these vulnerabilities, we propose a Bayesian Trajectory Monitoring framework, integrating global context and local segment evidence to detect covert misalignment. Empirically, our method significantly consolidates monitor robustness with 0.91 AUC and 0.74 TPR@FPR=0.05.

title: Fine-Tuning a Transducer for Impaired Speech: Where the Gains Appear and What They Mean for Evaluation
summary: Speech recognition still works poorly for many people whose speech is affected by conditions such as ALS, Parkinson's disease, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome or stroke. We took part in the Speech Accessibility Project Challenge 2 (SAPC2) with a public speech recognizer that we fine-tuned on the challenge data. Our best entry scored 7.81% character error rate on Test1, the first of two hidden test sets (official baseline 15.26%). Our live entries ran on CPUs with a combined median latency of about 0.9 seconds at 7.96-8.07% error. On new speakers, fine-tuning reduced errors most for the speakers that an off-the-shelf recognizer finds hardest to understand. Sentences already seen in training had far lower error rates than new ones (2.58% vs 6.42%), a larger difference than being a familiar speaker made. We close with lessons for evaluating such systems.

title: The Gating Mechanism of KV Cache Eviction
summary: KV cache eviction must decide which entries carry information that the rest of the cache can no longer supply. A natural way to estimate this is a learnable gate: give each cached entry a gate on its attention weight and train the gate on the model's own objective. The gate belongs inside the normalizing softmax, where suppressing one entry hands its mass to the others rather than discarding it. That same normalizer absorbs any per-query constant, so a constant gate cancels and reproduces the frozen model exactly. Trained on the language-modeling loss the gate stays near a constant score while its loss falls throughout: optimization succeeds, but a frozen backbone was fit for dense attention, so its loss prefers the no-op, and a near-constant score ranks nothing. The no-op is not a floor the gate improves from but what its objective asks for. A second obstacle survives once the gate moves, since the same gradient charges the gate for errors the frozen model already makes, which no reweighting of positions separates out. Much of the machinery in learnable eviction, from sparsity penalties to relaxations of the discrete decision, works around the first obstacle rather than removing it; both are removed by putting dense attention beyond the gate's reach and making the dense model's predictions its target. Under these two conditions capacity is never the missing ingredient: neither a larger scorer, nor explicit access to the past, nor a trainable backbone helps. The same holds for what eviction unavoidably discards, which is recovered by parameter-free centroids read inside the same softmax far better than by any memory read outside it, since the mass they must return is a share of that normalizer and available nowhere else. At 75\% KV cache compression, this gate reaches 90.14 on RULER at 8K and 46.03 on LongBench with Qwen3-8B, 3.72 and 1.36 points below full-cache inference.

title: English Calibration Erodes Lithuanian in Expert-Pruned Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
summary: A study investigates how English calibration data impacts the performance of expert-pruned Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models when applied to low-resource languages like Lithuanian.

title: Continued Training of Continuous Language Flows with Token Identity Squared Supervision
summary: This research explores continued training methods for continuous language flow models, extending diffusion and flow models to language modeling for text generation through continuous denoising in token embedding spaces.

title: O$^2$PD: Overlap-Gated On-Policy Distillation on Reliable Prefix
summary: The O$^2$PD method introduces overlap-gated on-policy distillation using a reliable prefix, providing dense token-level supervision to align a student model with a teacher's next-token distribution during its generated rollouts.

title: Evaluating Token Probabilities as Confidence Estimators in Human Behavior Simulations: A Case Study in Luxembourgish Next Like Prediction
summary: This paper evaluates token probabilities as confidence estimators for assessing the operational validity of large language models (LLMs) in human behavior simulations, using a case study in Luxembourgish next like prediction.

title: Extending Reasoning in Typed Decision Models via Looping
summary: A new method extends reasoning in typed decision models by introducing a looping mechanism for a block of layers, allowing more test-time compute in latent space without increasing parameters.

title: Automated Video-to-QA Pipeline: End-to-End Question Generation and Verification Using Large Language Models
summary: Researchers propose an end-to-end automated pipeline that utilizes large language models to extract structured summaries and generate high-fidelity questions and answers from video content.

title: Bridging Structure and Semantics: Knowledge Graph Verification via Triple-to-Text Alignment
summary: This paper introduces GenVer, a generative verifier that leverages pre-trained language models to perform knowledge graph verification by scoring triple-to-text alignments, thus improving semantic accuracy.

title: Dataset Collection and Fine-Tuning of NLLB for German--English Translation
summary: This study details the curation of a high-quality parallel corpus from OPUS Books and the subsequent fine-tuning of Meta's NLLB-200 models for improved German-English translation.

title: Decodability Is Not Validity: Evaluating Nuisance Sensitivity in Language Model Concept Probes
summary: This research evaluates the validity of language model concept probes, demonstrating that decodability does not equate to validity and investigating nuisance sensitivity in different target-nuisance settings.

title: Different Corpora, Different Skills? A Paired Study of Small Language Models
summary: A paired study investigates how the choice of pretraining corpus impacts the skills and capabilities of small language models, comparing two distinct corpora at matched data budgets.

title: Axis-LoRA: Probing and Adapting Embedding Models for Personal-Memory Retrieval
summary: Axis-LoRA is introduced as a method to probe and adapt embedding models for personal-memory retrieval, addressing the limitation of current models in distinguishing memories by time, place, person, and event for LLM-based systems.

title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
summary: The paper introduces 'Drex' as a step towards Foundation Decision Models, addressing inconsistencies and parsing challenges faced by autoregressive large language models in production.

title: Do Recommenders Need to Think in Words? Latent Reasoning for Efficient LLM-Based Recommendation
summary: This research investigates the efficiency of LLM-based recommender systems, questioning whether generating chain-of-thought text is necessary for reasoning or if latent reasoning can be more efficient.

title: CardioLM: A multilingual suite of small language models for the cardiology domain
summary: CardioLM is a new multilingual suite of small language models specifically developed for the cardiology domain to process clinical free-text documentation in various local languages.

title: Compression Through a Context Lens: Evaluating Adaptation, Quantization, and Distillation in Arabic Legal LLMs
summary: This study evaluates model compression techniques like adaptation, quantization, and distillation on Arabic Legal LLMs using the ArabLegalEval benchmark, focusing on their domain-specific performance in resource-constrained legal settings.

title: Automatic keyphrase extraction and annotation: modern theoretical approaches and practical solutions for text and speech
summary: This article provides a comprehensive analysis of modern theoretical approaches and practical solutions for automatic keyphrase extraction and annotation across both text and speech modalities.

title: Beyond K/V Caches: Cross-Model State Handoff in Hybrid Linear-Attention LLMs
summary: This work explores 'Cross-Model State Handoff' in hybrid linear-attention LLMs, addressing how context and accumulated state are efficiently transferred between different models during long conversations in production deployments.

title: Agent-R$^2$: Scaling Agents for Realistic Productivity Work via Real-Source Data Synthesis
summary: Agent-R$^2$ is a new approach that leverages real-source data synthesis to improve the scalability and performance of AI agents in tackling realistic, long-horizon productivity tasks.

title: From Twisted Facts to Rogue Agents: Can LLMs Reliably Detect Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations?
summary: This research introduces HaluCheck, a method for systematically evaluating and advancing post-generation hallucination detection in large language models, addressing their vulnerability to subtle and high-risk factual inaccuracies.

title: Terminal-style Mathematical Modeling Bench: The First Agentic and Verifiable Benchmark for Mathematical Modeling
summary: Introduces a new benchmark for mathematical modeling that is agentic and verifiable, aiming to evaluate how well AI systems can turn real-world problems into models, solutions, and defended recommendations.

title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
summary: Presents Multimodal-SEA, an interactive benchmark comprising 608 examples, designed to study the security of personal AI agents against multimodal social engineering attacks.

title: Measured Coupling for Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
summary: Proposes a new method for parallel decoding in diffusion language models that uses measured coupling to determine which tokens can be safely committed together, improving upon mean-field decoding.

title: LLM-Assisted Label Noise Correction for EEG-Based Sleep Stage Classification
summary: Introduces a method for automatic sleep stage classification from EEG signals that uses LLMs to correct label noise, aiming to improve the performance of deep learning models in clinical sleep medicine.

title: Polarity Classification with Multitask Learning Syntax Augmentation
summary: Describes a method for sentiment analysis that improves polarity classification by integrating multitask learning with syntax augmentation to handle linguistic phenomena like negation and intensification.

title: Cultural Adaptation within Repeated Social Interactions
summary: Investigates cultural adaptation in LLMs used as interactive agents, emphasizing the need to assess their cultural competence through repeated social interactions rather than just knowledge-based approaches.

title: SpecCTMC: Exact Speculative Simulation of Diffusion Language Model Continuous-Time Markov Chains
summary: Introduces SpecCTMC, a method for exact speculative simulation of continuous-time Markov chains in masked diffusion language models to enable parallel text generation without disrupting token dependencies.

title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
summary: Proposes MedGraph, a graph-based memory system for LLM-based medical assistants to accurately maintain a patient's clinical state across multiple visits in long-term medical dialogues.

title: Batch-Conditioned Semantic Anchors for Robust Transductive Adaptation of Vision--Language Models
summary: Introduces batch-conditioned semantic anchors to improve the robustness of transductive adaptation for vision-language models, mitigating issues like drift when processing sparse or diverse data batches.

title: TraCE: Trajectory-Aware Concepts for Explainable Video Understanding
summary: Presents TraCE, a method that uses trajectory-aware concepts to provide more precise and source-specific explanations for video understanding models, addressing limitations in current video XAI techniques.

title: Expanding the Quality-Coverage Frontier with Competitive Flow Matching
summary: Proposes Competitive Flow Matching to enhance flow matching (FM) generators, aiming to expand the quality-coverage frontier and overcome limitations associated with the quality-coverage tradeoff.

title: Segment What It Can Draw: Querying a Text-to-Image Generator with Its Own Images for Skin Lesion Segmentation
summary: Introduces a novel method for skin lesion segmentation without annotated masks by using a text-to-image diffusion transformer, querying it with its own generated images to specify the target.

title: SD-LoRA: Training-Time Structural Distillation into LoRA for Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation
summary: Presents SD-LoRA, a method that uses training-time structural distillation into LoRA for efficient few-shot adaptation of vision-language models, balancing fine-grained learning with deployment efficiency.

title: Wide View Synthesis from Overlapping Perspective Cameras in Autonomous Driving
summary: Formulates and addresses the problem of wide view synthesis in autonomous driving, aiming to create a unified wide view from spatially separated observations provided by multi-perspective camera systems.

title: A Proxy-Based Method for Measuring Racial Disparities in~Text-to-Image~Generators
summary: Presents an automated, proxy-based method for auditing text-to-image generators to measure racial disparities and representational bias against ground-truth demographic benchmarks.

title: Perceptual Distortion for Overfitted Video Coding: Sliced Matching in Space, Error Alignment in Time
summary: Explores perceptual distortion in neural video coding, proposing a method that uses sliced matching in space and error alignment in time, leveraging Wasserstein Distortion to balance quality and fidelity.

title: VINO: Revisiting 3D Representation Learning with Volume Transformers
summary: Introduces VINO, a new approach that revisits 3D representation learning using Volume Transformers to address limitations in current 3D representation methods and achieve general-purpose scene representations.

title: Householder Motion Embedding: Noise Modulation for Motion-Controllable Video Generation
summary: Proposes Householder Motion Embedding, a noise modulation method that enhances precise motion control in diffusion models for video generation, overcoming limitations of standard spatiotemporal noise warping.

title: ArtiVidRM: Verifiable Artifact-as-Rubric Reward Modeling for Explicit Quality Articulation in Video Generation
summary: Introduces ArtiVidRM, a verifiable artifact-as-rubric reward modeling approach for video generation that uses reinforcement learning to explicitly articulate and improve video quality.

title: Where Do Reported Long-Video QA Gains Come From? A Controlled Audit of Frame Selection, Evidence Injection, and Expert Routing
summary: Presents VideoRouteAudit, a controlled audit to analyze the sources of performance gains in long-video question answering by disentangling the effects of frame selection, non-visual evidence injection, and model routing.

title: MIKU: Material Invariance and Knowledge Unification for PBR Generation
summary: MIKU is a new method for generating high-quality materials for physically based rendering (PBR), addressing issues with inconsistent representations in datasets and synthesis pipelines.

title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
summary: WeLM-Image is a unified image foundation model designed for single-GPU deployment, integrating multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis.

title: Vis2State: Visual Reasoning through Executable State Abstractions
summary: Vis2State introduces a method for visual reasoning through executable state abstractions to solve visual puzzles by separating visual interpretation from task-specific rule computation.

title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs' Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning
summary: PSGAgent enhances Multimodal Large Language Models' (MLLMs) visual perception for Panoptic Scene Graph generation by employing agentic reasoning to overcome static observation limitations.

title: TRiST: Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer for Medical Image Analysis
summary: TRiST (Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer) is a new architecture for medical image analysis that explicitly incorporates topological patterns from medical images into its multiscale representations.

title: Compact Motion Embeddings for Feed-forward Unified Human Animation
summary: This research proposes a method for creating compact motion embeddings to achieve feed-forward unified human animation, capturing articulation without the driver's appearance.

title: Coverage Hides Churn: Auditing and Preserving Conformal Decisions as VLM Label Registries Grow
summary: This paper reveals that adding new labels to vision-language classifiers can silently alter conformal decisions about old labels and proposes methods for auditing and preserving these decisions.

title: Concertina: Embodying Manipulation and Cognition in One Diffusion Vision-Language Model
summary: Concertina is a new diffusion Vision-Language Model designed for manipulation, aiming to integrate manipulation and cognition within a single embodied AI framework, unlike decoupled existing policies.

title: Action-Conditioned VLM Monitoring for Autonomous Vehicle Semantic Anomalies
summary: This research investigates action-conditioned Vision-Language Model monitoring to evaluate the appropriateness of autonomous vehicle behavior in semantically unusual driving scenes.

title: OptIMerge: Optimization-Based Merging of Diffusion Models
summary: OptIMerge introduces an optimization-based method for merging weights of multiple diffusion models, aiming to improve multi-task learning beyond simple arithmetic averaging.

title: Training-Free Predictive Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Few-Step Autoregressive Video Diffusion
summary: This work proposes a training-free predictive spatio-temporal token pruning method to accelerate few-step autoregressive video diffusion models towards real-time generation.

title: Improving Long-Tail Detection via Layout-Instruction Conditioned Diffusion Synthesis
summary: Tail-SD is a new layout-instruction conditioned stable diffusion framework proposed to improve long-tail object detection by generating more effective synthetic data for rare classes.

title: MetricTrail: Revisiting the Power of Metric Depth and Local Optimization for Long-Sequence Streaming 3D Reconstruction
summary: MetricTrail is a streaming system presented for accurate camera motion estimation and dense 3D reconstruction from long monocular videos, enhancing efficiency with metric depth and local optimization.

title: Guidance Is a Field, Not a Scalar: Interval-Integrated Classifier-Free Guidance for One-Step Video Generation
summary: This paper introduces interval-integrated classifier-free guidance, treating guidance as a field rather than a scalar, to improve one-step video generation by MeanFlow-based generators.

title: Georeferenced Cross-View 3D Reconstruction from Ground and Satellite Images
summary: This research focuses on georeferenced 3D reconstruction from ground and satellite images, aiming to recover local scene geometry and localize all points in a geographic coordinate frame.

title: Subspace Learning with Outlier Exposure for Out-of-Distribution Detection
summary: This paper explores subspace learning with outlier exposure to enhance out-of-distribution (OoD) detection, crucial for reliable deployment of deep neural networks.

title: TACT-KV: Tri-Axis Cosine Transform for Compressing Volumetric KV Caches in Medical VLMs
